posts.title: Pereiaslav Council (1654)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Pereiaslav Council (1654) (C0001)

The oath of Bohdan Khmelnytsky and the starshyna to the tsar. Establishment of control over the Hetmanate through a legal trap: the treaty was asymmetric by design – in response to the demand for a mutual oath, envoy "V. Buturlin, citing the autocratic character of the Russian monarch's power, refused to do so"[1]. The very language of "reunification" is a later imperial overlay: Tsar Aleksei's charter to the Zaporozhian Host (27 March 1654) speaks only of subjects who "have come under our sovereign's high hand"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Sham Treaties (T0088)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/360):** The Tsardom of Muscovy exploited the critical position of the Hetmanate to impose a format of subordination, refusing from the outset to take on symmetrical obligations. To the Cossacks' demand for a mutual oath the tsar's envoy answered with a refusal - by the embassy's own report, swearing on behalf of the sovereign was "a thing that has never happened and never will, and it is unbecoming for the hetman even to say such things, for every subject must swear to his sovereign"[3]; Khmelnytsky had to convene the council three times in a single day, 18 (8) January 1654, yet Buturlin, citing the autocratic character of the Russian monarch's power, refused a second time[1]. The "treaty" itself was not a bilateral act: "The originals of the treaty documents have not survived. Only their copies and drafts are known"; the Ukrainian side submitted its terms "in the form of petitions to the tsar," while "the acts of the tsarist government took the form of 'grants' from the tsar"[4] - the written terms were drawn up only in Moscow in March 1654. |
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The seizure of a neighboring state's territories was presented to the population of the Tsardom of Muscovy not as an act of political or military expansion, but as a sacred mission of protecting brothers in faith. This myth outlived the centuries: as late as 1990 Solzhenitsyn reproduced it verbatim – "The return of these lands to Russia was then perceived by everyone as REUNIFICATION"[5]. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** From the very beginning, Moscow laid an asymmetric foundation for the relationship, harshly cutting off the autonomy's international agency. Tsar Aleksei's charter directly restricted the hetman's foreign relations: "And with the Turkish sultan and the Polish king, without our tsarist majesty's decree, no relations are to be maintained"[2]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

1. Редкол.: В. А. Смолій (голова) та ін. НАН України. Інститут історії України. (2011). Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8.
2. Царь Алексей Михайлович (Акты ЮЗР, т. X, с. 489–494). (1654). Жалованная грамота царя Алексея Михайловича Войску Запорожскому.
3. Михайло Грушевський (кн. 2: Хмельниччини роки 1654–1657; переказ статейного списку посольства В.Бутурліна за Актами ЮЗР, т. X). (1931). Історія України-Руси: Т. IX.
4. Редкол.: В. А. Смолій (голова) та ін. НАН України. Інститут історії України. (2003). Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1.
5. Александр Солженицын (Литературная газета, 18.09.1990). (1990). Как нам обустроить Россию?.

posts.title: Truce of Vilna (1656)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Truce of Vilna (1656) (C0002)

Separate peace negotiations between Moscow and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth on ending the war and dividing spheres of influence, held in complete isolation from the Ukrainian side: "The plenipotentiary representatives of the Ukrainian Cossack state, headed by R. Haponenko, were not admitted to the negotiating table"[1]. The hetman asked that the Cossack envoys be given mandates as full participants of the congress - "but the tsar's government once again let this request pass unheeded," and the delegates "sat idle beside the commissioners, not admitted to the official sessions"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** As soon as political interests changed, Moscow went for a separate peace with its recent enemy – Poland – negotiating behind its Ukrainian ally's back: "The priorities at the negotiations were territorial and financial questions, as well as the terms of the election of the Russian tsar to the Polish throne"[1] – the fate of the Cossack lands became a bargaining chip in this deal. The negotiations were held at Niemieza near Vilna from August 1656; the armistice was signed on October 24[1]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The Tsardom of Muscovy physically and legally isolated the autonomy from participation in international politics, deciding the fate of the Cossack lands without regard for their national interests: "The plenipotentiary representatives of the Ukrainian Cossack state, headed by R. Haponenko, were not admitted to the negotiating table"[1]. The hetman's request to grant the envoys mandates as full participants was "let pass unheeded" by the tsar's government: the delegates "sat idle beside the commissioners, not admitted to the official sessions"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Muscovite–Ukrainian War (1658–1659)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Muscovite–Ukrainian War (1658–1659) (C0003)

Open military aggression by the Tsardom of Muscovy in response to the hetman's attempt to break vassalage. It was accompanied by the fomenting of civil war through sponsorship of the opposition – the revolt of Pushkar and Barabash against Vyhovsky[1] – and by a direct invasion of the Muscovite army, which suffered catastrophic losses at Konotop: "The flower of the Muscovite cavalry, which had made the fortunate campaigns of '54 and '55, perished in a single day"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Proxy War (T0018)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/326):** Seeking to weaken the Hetmanate from within and prevent it from breaking vassalage, Moscow artificially fomented civil war, supporting and arming the internal opposition against the lawful hetman: "The proclamation of I. Vyhovsky as hetman was received negatively by the representatives of the forces opposed to him," led by Poltava colonel Pushkar and kish otaman Barabash[1]. Their revolt opened the period of the bloody Ruin. |
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** When covert methods of destabilization proved insufficient, the tsardom moved to open military invasion. The regular Muscovite army tried to subdue the Hetmanate by force, which ended in catastrophe at Konotop. The imperial historian Soloviev admitted: "The flower of the Muscovite cavalry, which had made the fortunate campaigns of '54 and '55, perished in a single day… Never again was the tsar of Muscovy able to field such a strong host"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Pereiaslav Articles (1659)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Pereiaslav Articles (1659) (C0004)

The imposition of a new enslaving treaty on Yurii Khmelnytsky under the pressure of Muscovite troops. The treaty abolished independence: "the Ukrainian state lost its independence and acquired the status of a political autonomy within the Russian state"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Taking advantage of the political crisis and having surrounded the autonomy's leaders with its troops, the tsardom forced them to sign a new, utterly enslaving treaty. The articles turned the confederative bond with Moscow into a federative one: "the Pereiaslav Articles converted Ukraine's confederative ties with Russia into the form of a federation. The Ukrainian state lost its independence and acquired the status of a political autonomy within the Russian state"[1]. The very basis of the treaty was forged: "Prince Trubetskoy took advantage of his military superiority over Yu. Khmelnytsky, rejected the Zherdiv Articles and forced the Ukrainian side to accept 14 points of the so-called old articles of 1654 (which in reality constituted a falsification of the 1654 treaty)"[1]. The 14 imposed points themselves are published in the "Collection of State Charters and Treaties"[2]. |
| **[Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel (T0041)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** After forcing the signing of the treaty, Moscow moved to the direct occupation of the autonomy's living space. The articles codified the expansion of the military presence: "besides Kyiv, tsarist voivodes were introduced into Pereiaslav, Chernihiv, Nizhyn, Bratslav, and Uman"[1] – garrisons headed by voivodes ensured physical control over the territory from within. |

</details>

posts.title: Truce of Andrusovo (1667)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Truce of Andrusovo (1667) (C0005)

An agreement on the partition of the Hetmanate along the Dnipro between the Tsardom of Muscovy and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth without Ukrainian participation: "The Russian state received significant territorial acquisitions… However, Right-Bank Ukraine, Polotsk, Vitebsk, and other Belarusian cities with Russian garrisons remained with the Commonwealth"[1]. The legal entrenchment of Ukraine's split and the transformation of Zaporizhzhia into a buffer zone: "under the treaty of 1667 it was under the joint rule of Moscow and Warsaw"[2]. Hrushevsky records the reaction to the partition: "there was great resentment against the Muscovite government for agreeing to cede Right-Bank Ukraine to Poland in the armistice of 1667: it divided Ukraine with Poland and did not keep what it had promised when taking Ukraine under the tsar's hand"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The official partition of Ukrainian lands between two neighboring states. The treaty was signed exclusively by representatives of Moscow and Warsaw: "Concluded on January 30 (February 9) in the village of Andrusovo, near Smolensk, for 13.5 years. The Russian delegation was headed by okolnichy A. L. Ordin-Nashchokin, the Polish one by commissioner Yu. Hlebowicz"[1]. The opinion of the autonomy itself was completely ignored: "The interests of the hetmans and of Ukraine were, of course, not taken into account"[4]. A separate knot of the collusion was Kyiv: article 7 of the Andrusovo treaty (30 January 1667) stipulated that "the very city of Kyiv… is to be handed over and vacated… that is, within two years, counting from the present treaty… in the coming year 1669, on the 15th day of April"[5]; "Muscovy then did not give it back"[3] - and in 1686 it legalized what it had withheld, "paying for Kyiv once more" (see the "Eternal Peace" campaign). The "territory for money" scheme was laid down in the same document: article 34 records Tsar Aleksei's consent to grant "a worthy treasury for the satisfaction of the szlachta exiles… from the part of Ukraine ceded to His Tsarist Majesty's side"[5] - with the sum deferred to future embassies. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** In the legal partition of Ukrainian lands, the opinion of the people themselves or of their leaders was demonstratively ignored. The Hetmanate was treated exclusively as an object: "The interests of the hetmans and of Ukraine were, of course, not taken into account"[4]. |
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The legal codification of the territory's division. Moscow deliberately fragmented a once unified country, turning such important regions as Zaporizhzhia into rightless buffer zones under joint administration: "...Zaporizhzhia (which under the treaty of 1667 was under the joint rule of Moscow and Warsaw)"[2]. |
| **[Taxation (T0056)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/355):** Having gained political power over the Left Bank, Moscow immediately attempted to seize the right to collect taxes in order to extract resources directly: "the attempts of Russian voivodes... to introduce their own taxation system in Ukraine led only to revolts (for example... the attempted census of 1666...)"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Publication of the "Synopsis" (1674)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Publication of the "Synopsis" (1674) (C0006)

The creation of the first large-scale ideological justification for the seizure of lands by the Muscovite tsars – the "Synopsis, or a Brief Collection from Various Chroniclers on the Origin of the Slaveno-Rossian People," published by the printing house of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra in 1674[1]. The author's calculation was political: "to give the Muscovite tsar the motivation to continue the struggle with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth for the liberation from Catholic rule of the remaining part of the 'single Orthodox people'"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Rewriting of History (T0004)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** For the ideological justification of the seizure, the Muscovite authorities received a ready-made historical canon: "the 'SYNOPSIS,' 'Synopsis, or a Brief Collection from Various Chroniclers on the Origin of the Slaveno-Rossian People' – a historical work first published by the printing house of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra (1674)"[1] – the book constructed a shared "Slaveno-Rossian" past, legitimizing Moscow's rule over Kyiv retroactively. |
| **[Imposition of Its Own Picture of Reality (T0007)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/317):** The implantation of a narrative about the unbreakable bond between Kyiv and Moscow, serving the political aims of the metropole: the author sought "to give the Muscovite tsar the motivation to continue the struggle with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth" and "to ease the incorporation of the Hetmanate's elite into the Russian ruling estate"[2]. |
| **[Denial of a Distinct Identity (T0010)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The deliberate dissolution of a distinct Ukrainian identity in the construct of a "single Orthodox people": the "Synopsis" subordinated Kyiv's history to the idea of a common "Slaveno-Rossian people"[1], and its political program presupposed a struggle for the "liberation… of the remaining part of the 'single Orthodox people'"[2]. Hrushevsky points out what exactly was erased: the "Synopsis" is "a brief history of Rus composed at the Pechersk Lavra, done very lifelessly and incompletely (the history of the Cossacks, the struggle against Poland, and all of Ukraine's recent history are almost entirely omitted from it)"[3]. |
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The imperial historical myth was directly based on religious manipulation: expansion was justified by the concept of religious unity. The author constructed an ideologeme in order "to give the Muscovite tsar the motivation to continue the struggle with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth for the liberation from Catholic rule of the remaining part of the 'single Orthodox people'"[2]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

posts.title: Kolomak Articles (1687)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Kolomak Articles (1687) (C0007)

Another stage of the assault on autonomy: a treaty with Moscow that eliminated independent diplomacy ("a hetman shall not be elected... nor shall they write anything to anyone on their own behalf"), prohibited declaring one's own subjecthood, and demanded: "to unite the Little Russian people with the Great Russian people by all measures and means... through marriage"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** The systematic dismantling of the autonomy's democratic institutions. Moscow categorically forbade the Cossacks to elect their leaders independently and to conduct an independent foreign policy: "and without a petition and without a decree of the great sovereigns... a hetman shall not be elected... nor shall they, on their own... write anything to anyone"[1]. The abolition of the historical right to grant asylum: the autonomy was forced to perform the functions of the Muscovite punitive apparatus and to hand over fugitives: "and those fugitives and people of all ranks shall not be received, nor kept among them"[1]. |
| **[Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel (T0041)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** To ensure constant armed oversight of the autonomy's top leadership and to prevent uprisings, the Tsardom of Muscovy stationed its regular troops directly in the hetman's capital: "with the hetman in Baturyn, for his protection and safety, there shall be a Muscovite streltsy regiment..."[1]. |
| **[Denial of a Distinct Identity (T0010)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The introduction of strict political censorship. Under threat of punishment, the population was forbidden even to say aloud that their lands constituted a separate state entity: "and let no one utter such voices, that the Little Russian land is of the hetman's regiment"[1]. |
| **[Encouragement of Mixed Marriages (T0117.002)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/390):** The use of demographic engineering to accelerate assimilation. Moscow openly proclaimed a course toward erasing ethnic boundaries by encouraging marriages with Great Russians: "to unite the Little Russian people with the Great Russian people by all measures and means... through matrimony and other conduct..."[1]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** "In this provision of the articles, the tsarist government's aspiration to turn Ukraine into a region incorporated into the Russian state on ordinary terms was openly declared for the first time"[2]. |
| **[Cultural Assimilation (T0115)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/380):** The Tsardom of Muscovy enshrined in state documents its course toward the complete absorption of the region: "Prince Vasily declared in the articles the beginning of the process of Russification"[2]. |
| **[Bribery of Elites (T0015)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/324):** To guarantee acceptance of the treaty's enslaving terms, the tsardom bribed the local starshyna with guarantees that they would keep their offices, placing the elite's personal ambitions above national ones: "the hetman shall not remove anyone of the general starshyna from office without the will and decree of their most serene tsarist majesty..."[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Annexation of the Kyiv Metropolis by the Moscow Patriarchate (1685–1690)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Annexation of the Kyiv Metropolis by the Moscow Patriarchate (1685–1690) (C0008)

The annexation of the independent Ukrainian church through diplomatic pressure and corruption. Patriarch Dositheus of Jerusalem directly accused the Muscovite envoys of simony: "What fault is it to tear away another's eparchy? Is it not a shame before people, is it not a sin before God! You send money and lead people out of their minds, you take charters contrary to the church and to God"[1]. The subordination of the church was justified by geopolitics: "Golitsyn's main project… was the reform of the Ukrainian Orthodox church, or rather – the subordination of the Kyiv metropolitanate to the Moscow patriarch"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Bribery of Elites (T0015)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/324):** To gain control over the church, Moscow applied corruption at the international level: the Kyiv metropolitanate was seized "through bribery, manipulation, and blackmail"[3]. The payment was recorded by Patriarch Dionysius of Constantinople himself in a letter to the tsars: "We have received the alms of your holy tsardom from your envoy, lord Nikita Alekseevich – three forties of sables and two hundred gold pieces"[1]. |
| **[Seizure of Religious Institutions (T0100)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/362):** The liquidation of independent jurisdiction to turn the church into an instrument of assimilation – the annexation of the Ukrainian church to the Muscovite one in 1686[4]. The Ecumenical Patriarchate later officially stated that these actions "were carried out entirely out of accord with the lawful canonical prescriptions"[5]. |
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** The introduction of censorship control over Ukrainian book printing. Patriarch Joachim banned publications without his sanction and sent a reprimand for publishing books without prior permission[2][6], and in 1690 "the Council of the Russian Orthodox Church condemned the 'new Kyivan books' of Petro Mohyla, Kyrylo Stavrovetsky, Ioanykii Galiatovsky, Sylvestr Kosov, Lazar Baranovych, and others, laying on them a curse and anathema"[7]. |
| **[Destruction of Local Knowledge Systems (T0044)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/348):** The destruction of the Kyiv theological school and the declaration of its works as heresy: "All Ukrainian writings, beginning with the catechism of Petro Mohyla, were declared heretical... the council condemned virtually all the principal works of Kyivan theological scholarship"[6][2]. |
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The annexation of the metropolitanate was disguised as the protection of co-religionists: the reform was carried out "relying on the Orthodox movement against the Turkish conquerors"[2], and "Golitsyn's main project concerning Ukraine… became the reform of the Ukrainian Orthodox church, or rather – the subordination of the Kyiv metropolitanate to the Moscow patriarch"[2][6]. |
| **[Religious Assimilation (T0116)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/384):** Immediately after the subordination began the imposition of Muscovite church standards and rites, marginalizing the local tradition. The Ecumenical Patriarchate recorded the canonical illegality of the act itself directly: "the alienation from our Throne of the Metropolitanate of Kyiv and of the Orthodox Churches of Lithuania and Poland dependent on it, as well as their attachment to the Holy Church of Moscow, were from the very beginning carried out entirely out of accord with the lawful canonical prescriptions"[5]. |
| **[Ban on Worship in the Native Language (T0116.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/387):** Following the establishment of control over the metropolitanate came the gradual unification of liturgical printing and pronunciation along Muscovite models, culminating in Peter I's direct decree of 1720: church books could be printed only after being checked against Muscovite ones, "so that there be no discord or distinct dialect in them"[8]. |

</details>

posts.title: "Eternal Peace" with Poland (1686)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: "Eternal Peace" with Poland (1686) (C0009)

The legal legitimation of the partition of territories between the Tsardom of Muscovy and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth behind the Hetmanate's back, definitively turning Ukraine into a rightless object of bargaining. The deal was sealed financially – under the text of the 1686 treaty Moscow undertook "for eternal peace to count out a genuine sum of money, that is, one hundred forty-six thousand Muscovite rubles, and hand it over to the Commonwealth"[1]. "Russian historians usually assess the Eternal Peace as Golitsyn's great diplomatic success, Polish ones – as their major defeat, and contemporary Ukrainian ones – as a national tragedy of Ukraine"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The division of spheres of influence behind the Ukrainian ally's back, accompanied by a financial deal for territory: under the 1686 treaty Moscow undertook "to count out one hundred forty-six thousand Muscovite rubles and hand them over to the Commonwealth"[1][2][3]. Ukrainian historiography recorded the deal as an ordinary purchase - Hrushevsky: Muscovy "concluded an eternal accord with Poland (paying, in addition, another 146 thousand rubles for Kyiv)"[4]. |
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The legal codification of the country's split into two parts, with the Right Bank turned into a buffer zone: "Under the terms of the Eternal Peace, the Right Bank remained with Poland... it was agreed and resolved that those places are to remain deserted, as they now are"[3][2]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The complete exclusion of the autonomy from participation in international negotiations on the status of its own territories. In the legal partition of Ukrainian lands the opinion of the people themselves was ignored – contemporary Ukrainian historiography assesses the Eternal Peace "as a national tragedy of Ukraine"[2]. |
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The diplomatic entrenchment of spiritual expansion: Moscow secured the inclusion in the treaty of an article on the position of the Orthodox in the Commonwealth – the 1686 treaty ordered the Polish side "to inflict no oppression and no coercion toward the Roman faith or the Union"[1] – and arrogated to itself the role of protector of Orthodoxy on Polish lands, relying on the Kyiv metropolitanate already subordinated to Moscow. The treaty also secured an ecclesiastical lever: the Orthodox eparchies in the Commonwealth "according to their spiritual rank and custom, are to receive blessing and ordination from the Metropolitan of Kyiv; and this shall harm none of them in the favor of His Royal Majesty"[5] - while the Kyiv metropolitanate was already subordinated to Moscow. |

</details>

posts.title: Azov Campaigns and Fortress Construction (1695–1700)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Azov Campaigns and Fortress Construction (1695–1700) (C0010)

The use of the autonomy as a free resource and labor base for Peter I's ambitions in the south. The population bore extremely heavy logistical obligations: "Provisions for the volunteer troops were supplied by the commoners, who also stocked hay for the winter for the army's artillery." In addition, Moscow established military control by deploying a network of bases near the Zaporizhian Sich: "The Zaporozhians... put forward the demolition of Kamianyi Zaton as a condition for any oath... Mazepa was furious"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Taxation (T0056)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/355):** Shifting the financial and logistical burden of imperial wars onto the autonomy's shoulders: "The commoners supplied provisions for the volunteer troops, and they also stocked hay for the winter for the host's artillery"[1][2]. |
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The forced use of Cossacks to build imperial infrastructure under harsh conditions: "in the making of fortifications around the Kyiv-Pechersk Monastery"[1][2]. |
| **[Bribery of Elites (T0015)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/324):** The distribution of the highest imperial awards to buy the hetman's loyalty against the backdrop of Ukraine's resource exhaustion: Peter I "deigned to name me a knight of the glorious order of the holy first-called apostle of Christ, Andrew"[1][2]. |
| **[Construction of Fortresses (T0139)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/411):** The deployment of a network of military bases (Novobohorodytska, Kamianyi Zaton) near the Zaporozhian Sich. Under the pretext of protection, Moscow was establishing rigid military control: "The Zaporozhians... put forward the destruction of Kamianyi Zaton as a condition for any oath of allegiance"[1][2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708) (C0011)

Systematic exploitation of the Hetmanate's potential in a grueling war combined with the simultaneous launch of administrative absorption (the reforms of 1707). The Cossacks dispatched to distant fronts were «wearied, destitute, left horseless, and ruined by year-round military service». Orlyk relayed the starshyna's account of the plans to recut the autonomy: the empire was preparing «to convert the Cossacks into a regular army... to break the military rights and liberties» and «to take the Little Russian towns into its own domain»[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (6)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Forced Mobilization (T0049)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The dispatch of Cossack regiments to distant theaters of war (the Baltic lands, Poland), which led to their exhaustion. The troops were "wearied by year-round military service, impoverished, dismounted, destitute"[1][2]. |
| **[Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel (T0041)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** The strangulation of the autonomy's economy through the system of billeting the regular army: "And when the kompaniytsi and serdiuks stand in winter quarters... 24 commoners feed a single kompaniyets without any excuses"[1][2]. |
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The mass conscription of the population for the construction of military installations in Moscow's interests. The tsar officially thanked the hetman and the starshyna for their "diligent zeal (and considerable labors borne) in the making of the Pechersk fortification" and promised for this "service and labors in the making of the said fortification" his "most exalted favor"[1]. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Preparation for dismantling the autonomy during the reforms of 1707: by Orlyk's account, the Cossack starshyna expected the empire to be preparing "to turn the Cossacks into a regular army… to break the rights and liberties of the Host"[1][2]. |
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** Preparation for the liquidation of the Hetmanate through the gubernia reform, into which Cossack towns were artificially inscribed. Moscow planned "to take the Little Russian towns into its own domain"[1][2]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** A course toward the complete absorption and destruction of the very name of the Cossack state. In the Bendery Constitution of 1710, Orlyk recorded Moscow's intention "to eradicate the Zaporozhian Host of the Lower Dnipro and to efface its name forever"[1]. Hrushevsky confirms the course was systemic: Mazepa's alliance with the Swedish king merely "gave the Muscovite government occasion… to take up more forcefully the abolition of Ukrainian autonomy. The Muscovite government had pursued this line from the very beginning"[3]. What was at stake was the enslavement of the entire people: the Muscovite state, per the preamble of Orlyk's constitution, managed to "violate and utterly destroy" the rights and liberties "and to cast a slave's yoke upon the free Cossack people, never conquered by it"[4]. |

</details>

posts.title: Mazepa's Defection to Sweden and the Baturyn Massacre (1708)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Mazepa's Defection to Sweden and the Baturyn Massacre (1708) (C0012)

In response to the autonomy's attempt to break vassalage, the regular Muscovite army destroyed the hetman's capital, Baturyn. Peter ordered: "and Baturyn, as a sign to the traitors (since they resisted), burn down entirely as an example to others"[1]. The reprisal was accompanied by terror against the civilian population: "Funck slaughtered more than a thousand people in the small town of Terey (Tereyska sloboda) and burned the town down"[2], and in total "about 15 thousand Ukrainians died in the Baturyn tragedy, including all the women and children"[1]. The massacre ran in parallel with propaganda: "Tsarist letters were circulated among the people claiming that Mazepa had gone over to the Swedes in order to hand Ukraine to Poland, to introduce the Union in Ukraine and eradicate the pious faith; that he was an apostate, a secret Catholic"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (9)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Punitive Expeditions (T0077)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** The deployment of the regular army to physically destroy the Hetmanate's defiant capital: "On the morning of November 2, Russian troops burst into Baturyn. After a two-hour battle, the remnants of the garrison were slaughtered together with the entire civilian population"[1][4]. The town was looted and burned on Peter's direct order - his letter to Menshikov of 5 November 1708: "and Baturyn, as a mark against the traitors (for they resisted), burn entire, as an example to others"[5]. |
| **[Extermination on a Territorial Basis (T0118)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/391):** Total massacre of the civilian population: "Funck slaughtered more than a thousand people in the small town of Terey and burned the town down, and also burned Dryhalov (Nedryhailiv)… and ordered everyone encountered to be killed, so as to instill horror in others"[2]. "In total, about 15 thousand Ukrainians died in the Baturyn tragedy, including all the women and children"[1][4]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** The demonstrative destruction of the city as an act of intimidation for the rest of the country. Peter I personally gave the order: "and Baturyn, as a sign to the traitors, burn down entirely as an example to others"[1][4]. Hrushevsky: the Muscovite army, having taken Baturyn "through the treachery of one man," "dealt terribly with the populace: the people were slaughtered, the town razed to the ground, the commanders given over to terrible tortures"[3]. |
| **[Destruction of Historical Memory (T0045)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** A campaign to erase the resistance leader's name (damnatio memoriae): "For two centuries the name and deeds of Mazepa were expunged… His coats of arms were knocked off the churches he had built, his name was painted over in books"[1][4]. |
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The use of the subordinated church to legitimize the reprisal through a political anathema. The Ecumenical Patriarchate never recognized it: "the anathema was laid on Ivan Mazepa for political reasons and had no theological or canonical justification"[6]. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** Large-scale looting of state arsenals and the treasury during the punitive raid on the autonomy's capital: "Menshikov managed to remove part of the artillery"[1][4]; the remaining guns were blown up and the city burned. |
| **[Theft of Cultural Property (T0112)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/372):** Deliberate removal of intellectual and historical heritage. The imperial troops did not merely loot — they seized unique documents: "Menshikov managed to carry off... the hetman's archive and Mazepa's library"[1][4]. |
| **[Puppet Government (T0037)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/342):** The installation of a government fully controlled by Moscow after the destruction of the capital: the election of the new hetman took place in Peter's presence immediately after the execution of the Baturyn officers – "Under the circumstances, the officers simply confirmed Skoropadsky, presented by Peter"[1]. Hrushevsky records the mechanics of dependence: "The hetman's residence was moved from Baturyn to Hlukhiv, right up against the Muscovite border, and two Muscovite regiments were garrisoned there so that the residents could arrest the hetman and the officers at once," and "everyone in Ukraine understood that power lay not with the hetman but with those residents"[3]. |
| **[Sham Expression of Popular Will (T0109)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** The formalization of the occupation regime through sham procedures. The officers, terrorized by the massacre, were made to vote for the metropole's preferred candidate: "At the end of this spectacle came the execution of the officers captured in Baturyn, and then the formal election of a new hetman. Under the circumstances, the officers simply confirmed Skoropadsky, presented by Peter"[1][4]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Lebedyn Executions (1708–1709)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Lebedyn Executions (1708–1709) (C0013)

A punitive campaign against Mazepa's supporters after the hetman went over to the Swedes. In January 1709 the headquarters of the tsar and Menshikov were at Lebedyn and Sumy, from where the investigation of the Cossack officers was conducted[1]. The model of intimidation was the destruction of the hetman capital: on 2 November 1708 Baturyn was taken by Menshikov's troops, "the town was razed to the ground and its inhabitants annihilated," and when in July 1709 the tsar permitted it to be resettled, he obliged the inhabitants to pay a special tax to the treasury "for treason"[2]. The punishment fell on everyone: "in the bloody massacre and fire a multitude of the town's defenders and inhabitants perished"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The destruction of the political leadership that supported the hetman: "the entire (!) general starshyna" followed Mazepa, and of the Left-Bank colonels only four remained loyal to the tsar[1]. The investigation of the officers was directed from the tsar's headquarters, where "being at Lebedyn and Sumy, Peter and Menshikov in January 1709" oversaw the reprisals[1]. The ecclesiastical punishment was arranged by the tsar's direct order - by a letter of 31 October 1708 (No. 2795) Peter I instructed metropolitan Stefan Yavorsky: "be pleased to have him, for such a deed of his, publicly cursed in the cathedral church..."[1][3]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Intimidation of the population by an exemplary reprisal against an entire town: during the capture of Baturyn "in the bloody massacre and fire a multitude of the town's defenders and inhabitants perished"[1], "the town was razed to the ground and its inhabitants annihilated," and the returning residents were charged a special tax "for treason"[2]. The devastation of the hetman capital also destroyed the state archive of the Hetmanate, which suffered "during the storming of Baturyn castle by A. Menshikov in 1708"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1709)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1709) (C0014)

A military operation of Muscovite troops to completely destroy the Zaporozhian (Chortomlyk) Sich as an autonomous military center in revenge for its support of Charles XII: "Having lost the proxy battle for Zaporizhzhia, Peter decided to follow the path of Baturyn — to destroy the Sich"[1]. Contemporaries recorded the empire's goal directly – Orlyk wrote that Moscow intended "to eradicate the Zaporozhian Host of the Lower Dnipro and to efface its very name forever"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Punitive Expeditions (T0077)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** A punitive expedition against the Sich to physically annihilate the Lower Dnipro Cossacks: "Three infantry regiments led by Colonel P. Yakovlev were sent there. Keleberda was the first to be taken and burned on April 16. A stubborn battle was fought for Perevolochna"[1]. The assault on the Sich itself lasted four days. The punitive force was guided by mercenary colonel Hnat Galagan: in "1709 he took part in the destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich, for which he received four villages on the Right Bank"[3]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Public executions of prisoners as intimidation: "Cossacks and officers were hanged, their heads were cut off, and the graves of old Zaporozhians were desecrated"[1]. The head of the acting otaman was demonstratively sent to Zaporizhzhia[1]. |
| **[Extermination on a Territorial Basis (T0118)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/391):** Total extermination of the defenders: when Perevolochna was taken, "All the Zaporozhians and inhabitants were killed (only 12 people were taken alive), and the neighboring kurins were also burned and slaughtered"[1]. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** Destruction of the military-economic base of the Lower Dnipro Cossacks. The Sich "was a kind of military base housing the fleet, artillery, and arsenal"[4] – all of this infrastructure was destroyed or seized during the assault. |
| **[Total Destruction of Infrastructure (T0105)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/366):** Complete destruction of the Sich's buildings and neighboring fortifications: "the neighboring kurins were also burned and slaughtered"; "All the buildings were destroyed, as Menshikov wrote: 'To lay waste all their places, so that this treasonous nest be utterly uprooted'"[1]. |
| **[Destruction of Historical Memory (T0045)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** The issuing of an official manifesto banning the very name of the Sich in any documents[2]. Physical destruction of memory: "the graves of old Zaporozhians were desecrated"[1]. |
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The use of the church as an instrument of punishment: the anathema was proclaimed by the tsar's direct order - "be pleased to have him, for such a deed of his, publicly cursed in the cathedral church..."[2]. No theological grounding was supplied for it, and part of the Ukrainian clergy refused to accept the rite: a former Lokhvytsia archpriest said during the proclamation of the anathema, "Our Mazepa is holy and will be in heaven, and your sovereign will not"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Battle of Poltava and the Final Defeat of the Hetmanate (1709)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Battle of Poltava and the Final Defeat of the Hetmanate (1709) (C0015)

The decisive battle of the Great Northern War, in the course of which the military backbone of Ukrainian autonomy was finally eliminated. The defeat of the Swedish-Cossack alliance allowed Moscow to move from suppressing uprisings to the systematic dismantling of the Hetmanate's political agency[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** Physical destruction of the armed forces of the supporters of independence in a general battle in order to eliminate the military potential of the resistance[1]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Mass executions of captured Cossacks after the capitulation at Perevolochna and Poltava for the final intimidation of the supporters of autonomy[1]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The liquidation of the autonomy's statehood and international agency as a result of the defeat of the Swedish-Ukrainian forces. The rout at Poltava set off an irreversible process of dismantlement: "In the hundred years after the famous Pereiaslav Council, Ukraine traveled the path from the 'Articles of Bohdan Khmelnytsky'… to the de facto liquidation of the autonomy and the hetmanate, to the country's transformation into an ordinary province of the Russian Empire"[1]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

posts.title: The Reshetylivka Articles (1709)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Reshetylivka Articles (1709) (C0016)

The first systematic campaign to dismantle treaty-based agency: instead of an equal interstate treaty – the tsar's "decisive" resolutions upon the hetman's petitionary articles. "The joint document, drawn up as a decree, was signed by state chancellor Count G. Golovkin"[1] - the signature "State Chancellor, Count Golovkin. Given at Kyiv, 31 July 1709" stands under the published act itself[2]. The articles "fully preserved the previously established control of the tsarist regime over local financing, the functioning of the administrative apparatus, the Cossack army, and foreign policy"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** Refusal to sign a treaty: the replacement of an equal agreement with the tsar's unilateral "resolutions." "The joint document, drawn up as a decree, was signed by state chancellor Count G. Golovkin"[1][2] – the autonomy ceased to be a party to a treaty. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Entrenchment of tsarist control over the autonomy's foreign policy: the articles "fully preserved the previously established control of the tsarist regime over… foreign policy"[1]. |
| **[Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel (T0041)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** Preservation of tsarist representatives' oversight of the hetmanate's administrative apparatus: the articles "fully preserved the previously established control of the tsarist regime over local financing and the functioning of the administrative apparatus"[1]. The institution of the tsar's resident was established alongside the hetman: "The first tsar's resident was stolnik A. Izmailov, who in his work was guided by official and secret tsarist articles"; the residents "were given the right to control the election and official appointments of representatives of the starshyna"[1]. |
| **[Economic Control (T0038)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/343):** Preservation of the center's control over the region's finances: the articles "fully preserved the previously established control of the tsarist regime over local financing"[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) (C0017)

The physical and economic exhaustion of the region through the transformation of the Cossack host into unpaid labor for imperial construction projects. The chief of these was the Ladoga Canal: Peter I handed the direction of the works to Münnich, while the digging itself "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and "on the construction works, tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[1]. In 1721 the acting hetman P. Polubotok "headed a 10,000-strong Cossack corps dispatched by order of Tsar Peter I to the construction of the Ladoga Canal"[2]. For the defiant there were also the Neva construction sites - as hard labor: captured Zaporozhians were "exiled to Sankt-Piterburkh to hard labor forever"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The mass mobilization of Cossack regiments for penal construction labor: the digging of the Ladoga Canal "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and there "tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[1]. In 1721 a "10,000-strong Cossack corps" headed by P. Polubotok was dispatched to the canal[2]; the works continued through 1721–23[4]. |
| **[Resource Exploitation (T0102)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/364):** Shifting the upkeep of the mobilized onto the subjects themselves: Cossacks dispatched to the imperial construction sites were left without supply and "suffer great want from hunger, having neither food for themselves, nor winter quarters, nor fodder for the horses"[3]. Workers for state construction the tsar simply ordered to be "taken from Ukraine, from those towns that are under your authority"[3], while at the works themselves people perished "from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[1]. |
| **[Installation of a New System of Governance (T0036)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** Removing Cossack regiments from the Cossack hierarchy and placing them under the direct command of imperial officials: Peter I handed the direction of the Ladoga Canal works to B.-C. Münnich, who "took over from Prince A. Menshikov the direction of the construction (digging) of the Ladoga Canal"[1]; Cossack corps were dispatched to these works "by order of Tsar Peter I"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Case of Pavlo Polubotok (1723)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Case of Pavlo Polubotok (1723) (C0018)

Peter I's establishment of the First Little Russian Collegium to seize governance from the hetman's administration: the collegium was created "as the highest appellate instance and the administrative-controlling organ of the Russian state structure in Ukraine"[1]. It was accompanied by the arrest of acting hetman Polubotok and the officers for defending the autonomy: "the officers submitted to Emperor Peter I yet another petition to close the Little Russian Collegium. After this, interrogations of Polubotok began in the Secret Chancellery, and on November 10, 1723 he was arrested and imprisoned in the Peter and Paul Fortress"[2], where the hetman died. The arrest order itself was never published as a separate act - the case was run by the Secret Chancellery; the circumstances were retrospectively set out in Empress Catherine I's manifesto of 8 February 1725: "it was ordered that the General Starshyna - Polubotok, Chernysh and Savych - be in St. Petersburg to answer for it"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Installation of a New System of Governance (T0036)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** The introduction of the collegium as a parallel organ of power to seize judicial and fiscal functions from the hetman's administration: it acted "as the highest appellate instance and administrative-controlling organ"[1], and "the Little Russian Collegium for the first time channeled Ukrainian finances into the tsar's treasury in full"[1]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The arrest of the acting hetman and officers in St. Petersburg for petitions defending autonomous rights. Peter was preparing a demonstrative reprisal: "Peter I planned to hold a show trial of Polubotok and his associates, accuse them of 'high treason,' and liquidate the Ukrainian autonomy. A special General Court was created for this purpose"[4]. Only the prisoner's death derailed the plan: the hetman "died on December 21, 1724 (O.S.) of pneumonia"[4]. |

</details>

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Creation of the Little Russian Prikaz (1663) (C0023)

Institutional substitution: Ukrainian affairs were handed over to a special agency in Moscow. The Little Russian Prikaz was founded "as one of the departments of the Ambassadorial Prikaz to administer Ukrainian affairs," and through it the tsarist government "exercised control over the political-administrative activity of the hetman's administration and the tsarist voivodes in Ukraine"[1] – the Hetmanate fell under the permanent departmental oversight of the metropole.

posts.title: The Moscow Articles of Ivan Briukhovetsky (1665)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Moscow Articles of Ivan Briukhovetsky (1665) (C0024)

The treaty that became the point of no return in the political, economic, and military absorption of the autonomy: "Under the Moscow Articles, direct control over the military-administrative and financial-economic life of Ukraine (except for the Cossack estate) passed into the hands of the tsarist voivodes"[1]. Garrisons headed by voivodes were introduced into new cities as far as Kodak, taxes went directly to the tsar's treasury, and the Kyiv metropolitanate was to be subordinated to the Moscow patriarch[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel (T0041)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** Expansion of the military occupation of the autonomy: in addition to reinforcing the garrisons of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Pereiaslav, and Nizhyn, "Russian military garrisons headed by voivodes were introduced into Poltava, Kremenchuk, Novhorod-Siverskyi, Oster, Kaniv, and other cities, as well as into Kodak in the Liberties of the Zaporozhian Host"[1] – the upkeep of the troops was placed on Ukrainian taxpayers. |
| **[Taxation (T0056)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/355):** Direct extraction of the autonomy's economic resources: "The collection of taxes from the Ukrainian population was entrusted to the tsarist administration. The collected funds were channeled into the tsar's treasury"[1]. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Depriving the autonomy of control over its own administrative and economic life: "direct control over the military-administrative and financial-economic life of Ukraine passed into the hands of the tsarist voivodes"[1] – the sovereign functions of the hetman's authority passed to representatives of the metropole. |

</details>

posts.title: The Konotop Articles of Ivan Samoilovych (1672)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Konotop Articles of Ivan Samoilovych (1672) (C0025)

A further curtailment of the Hetmanate's political agency and interference in the autonomy's internal affairs: "Overall, the Konotop Articles limited the hetman's power in favor of the officer oligarchy, and also narrowed the autonomy of the Hetmanate"[1]. The weakening of the hetman's power laid the ground for the growing influence of the Muscovite government over the autonomy's elites.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Interference in internal governance: "the hetman was deprived of the right to arbitrarily (without a hearing before the military court) issue orders for the execution or dismissal of his subordinates"[2] – personnel and judicial decisions were removed from the hetman's sole authority. The norm itself is older than this treaty: it was first fixed by the Konotop Articles of 1672 ("executed and removed from office… by the judgment and proof of the Host's court")[3]. |
| **[Bribery of Elites (T0015)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/324):** A wager on the estate interests of the officer class: "The Konotop Articles limited both the hetman's power and, accordingly, the autonomy of the Hetmanate, while significantly expanding the rights of the Cossack officers"[2] – by expanding the rights of the officer oligarchy at the hetman's expense, Moscow gained levers of influence over the autonomy through the hands of its own elite. |

</details>

posts.title: Liquidation of the Cossacks in Right-Bank Ukraine (1699)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Liquidation of the Cossacks in Right-Bank Ukraine (1699) (C0026)

The destruction of the Cossack regimental order on the Right Bank by a decision of the Polish Sejm of 1699, on lands that Moscow and Warsaw had divided along the Dnipro by the "Eternal Peace" of 1686. Colonel Palii "did not accept the decisions of the general Sejm of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth of 1699 banning the Cossacks on the Right Bank" and "contrary to the terms of the 'Eternal Peace' of 1686 pursued a policy of uniting the Right Bank and the Left Bank"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The backroom partition of Ukraine along the Dnipro: by the "Eternal Peace" of 1686 Moscow officially ceded the Right Bank to Warsaw, without the participation or consent of Ukrainians themselves. The fate of the Right-Bank Cossacks was decided by foreign capitals: the ban of 1699 implemented this partition, against which Palii's Cossacks, "contrary to the terms of the 'Eternal Peace' of 1686," continued the struggle to unite both banks[1]. |
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The abolition of the regimental-sotnia administrative order to serve the imperial partition of the lands: the Sejm of 1699 adopted the decision "banning the Cossacks on the Right Bank"[1]. |

posts.title: Pylyp Orlyk's Campaign in Right-Bank Ukraine (1711)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Pylyp Orlyk's Campaign in Right-Bank Ukraine (1711) (C0027)

A military-diplomatic attempt to restore Ukraine's independence by the forces of the emigration with the support of allies. The campaign failed because of a stab in the back: "the Tatars, disobeying Orlyk, scattered in raiding parties and began taking yasyr captives across Ukrainian villages"[1].

---

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The collapse of the anti-Moscow coalition from within: on the Right Bank, the Tatar allies betrayed the Cossacks and turned to seizing the civilian population – "the Tatars, disobeying Orlyk, scattered in raiding parties and began taking yasyr captives across Ukrainian villages"[1]. Orlyk himself wrote to the Swedish king: "What atrocities unheard of under the moon did the wild Tatars then commit!"[1]. |
| **[Implantation of Officials and Military Personnel (T0041)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/345):** The empire's forcible retention of the Right Bank: the Bila Tserkva fortress with its Muscovite garrison held out, and the campaign collapsed after the Tatars' betrayal – "Orlyk retreated without taking Bila Tserkva"[1], and his army disintegrated. |

posts.title: The Decisive Points (1728)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Decisive Points (1728) (C0028)

A unilateral imperial act imposed on hetman Danylo Apostol instead of the traditional bilateral treaty. While formally softening the regime of the Little Russian Collegium, the document entrenched harsh imperial restrictions on key points: "Article 19 forbids the hetman relations with other countries"[1], customs revenues went to the tsar's treasury, and personnel appointments were placed under the metropole's control.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** Rejection of the treaty format: instead of a bilateral agreement – the tsar's "decisive" resolutions upon the hetman's requests, issued in the form of a decree. The autonomy ceased to be a party to a treaty and received its rules of existence from above. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Complete diplomatic isolation of the autonomy: "Article 19 forbids the hetman relations with other countries. He was to acquaint the tsar's resident with letters received from abroad, forward their translations to the tsar's court, and meanwhile detain the envoys"[1]. |
| **[Economic Control (T0038)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/343):** Embedding the autonomy's finances into the imperial system: the revenues from the indukta (duty on imported goods) "were to be transferred to the tsar's treasury"[1], while the host treasury was managed by two general treasurers – a Ukrainian and an appointed Russian. |

</details>

posts.title: The Governing Council of the Hetman Government and the Lubny Treaty (1734–1750)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Governing Council of the Hetman Government and the Lubny Treaty (1734–1750) (C0029)

A long period of direct rule over the Left Bank without the election of a hetman. "The GOVERNANCE OF THE HETMAN'S GOVERNMENT was an organ of power created by the government of Russian empress Anna in 1734 after the death of hetman D. Apostol to govern Left-Bank Ukraine (the Hetmanate) and to prevent new hetman elections"; "in essence its head was the tsar's resident"[1]. At the same time the empire brought Zaporizhzhia back under control: "Anna amnestied the Zaporozhians and allowed them to return to the old Sich grounds (1734) and found the New Sich"[2] – on the eve of war with Turkey the Cossacks were being brought back as a military resource of the crown.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Installation of a New System of Governance (T0036)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** Blocking the election of a new leader and creating a hybrid administration for direct control: "The Governance included the tsar's resident in Ukraine, Prince O. Shakhovskoy, with 2 Russian officials… as well as general quartermaster Ya. Lyzohub with 2 Ukrainian officers"[1] – a formally equal collegium actually headed by the tsar's resident. |
| **[Forced Registration of Subjecthood (T0147)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/417):** The return of the Zaporozhian Sich under the empire's authority on the crown's terms: "For tactical reasons, in the course of preparations for the next Turkish war, Anna amnestied the Zaporozhians and allowed them to return to the old Sich grounds (1734) and found the New Sich"[2] – the amnesty formalized the Cossacks' passage under Russian authority with an obligation of military service. |
| **[Encouragement of Mixed Marriages (T0117.002)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/390):** Targeted demographic assimilation under Anna's secret decree of January 31, 1734 to governor Shakhovskoy: "that you with your skill, secretly and quietly, take special pains to divert the Little Russians from kinship… and to encourage them and skillfully bring them into kinship with… the Great Russian people"[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Liquidation of the Institution of the Hetmancy and the Second Little Russian Collegium (1764)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Liquidation of the Institution of the Hetmancy and the Second Little Russian Collegium (1764) (C0030)

The final abolition of political autonomy. Catherine II forced hetman Rozumovsky to renounce his office and by the decree of November 10, 1764 established an occupation administration: "we command our Senate, for the proper governance of Little Russia, to establish there a Little Russian Collegium, presided over by our general, Count Rumyantsev"[1]. The program had been set in advance in a secret instruction: "so that they become Russified and cease looking to the forest like wolves"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The final elimination of the office of the autonomy's leader: after Rozumovsky's forced abdication, Catherine II's decree of November 10, 1764 handed power to the Little Russian Collegium, whose president was instructed to act "with a governor's authority, that is, as our special plenipotentiary"[1]. Catherine II's instruction to procurator-general Vyazemsky (1764) stated the goal openly: "and when there is no hetman in Little Russia, one must strive that the very age and name of hetmans vanish"[2]. |
| **[Installation of a New System of Governance (T0036)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** The establishment of a direct imperial organ – the Second Little Russian Collegium: four Great Russian members, four Little Russian ones, headed by Rumyantsev with the powers of a governor-general; the Zaporozhian Sich was also transferred to its jurisdiction: "the Zaporozhian Sich, which was under the hetman's jurisdiction, shall now be administered by this Little Russian government"[1]. |
| **[Cultural Assimilation (T0115)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/380):** The monarch's secret instruction on the cultural digestion of the land: "Little Russia, Livonia, and Finland are provinces governed by the privileges confirmed to them… These provinces, as well as Smolensk, must by the easiest means be brought to the point where they become Russified and cease looking to the forest like wolves"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: Abolition of the Cossack Order in Sloboda Ukraine (1765)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Abolition of the Cossack Order in Sloboda Ukraine (1765) (C0031)

An imperial reform to liquidate the military-social structure of Sloboda Ukraine: "The conclusions of this investigation, with the participation of a Senate commission, led to the verdict of the Governing Senate on the liquidation of the autonomous order on December 16, 1764, and a series of experimental innovations approved by Catherine II's manifesto of July 28, 1765. On the basis of the Sloboda regiments the Sloboda-Ukrainian Governorate was formed, out of the military forces – 5 hussar regiments of the same names (see Hussars), and the bulk of the Cossack population was transferred to the category of military settlers"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The liquidation of Cossack administrative units and the introduction of imperial division: the report of the Shakhovskoy-Panin commission confirmed by the empress on December 16, 1764 and Catherine II's manifesto of July 28, 1765[2][3] – "On the basis of the Sloboda regiments the Sloboda-Ukrainian Governorate was formed"[1]. |
| **[Taxation (T0056)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/355):** Lowering the social status of the indigenous population for the purpose of economic extraction: "The Cossacks and their helpers were turned into military settlers and taxed with the poll tax," and those with the right to distill horilka "now had to pay… 95 kopecks per soul to the treasury"[4]. |
| **[Forced Mobilization (T0049)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The forced incorporation of the autochthonous armed forces into the imperial army: "The Sloboda Cossack regiments were abolished and in their place it was ordered to form 5 hussar regiments"[4]. |

posts.title: Russo-Turkish War and the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1768–1774)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Russo-Turkish War and the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1768–1774) (C0032)

The use of Ukrainian resources and Cossack regiments for victory over the Ottomans on the Danube. The diplomatic severing of Crimea from the Ottoman Empire through the recognition of a fictitious "independence": under Article III of the treaty, "All the Tatar peoples: the Crimean, Budjak, Kuban, Yedisan, Jamboyluk, and Yedichkul, without exception, are to be recognized by both empires as free and entirely independent of any outside power"[1] – this "independence" became the prologue to the annexation of the peninsula nine years later.

The merits of the Zaporozhians and their kish otaman Kalnyshevsky in this war "were recognized by the tsarist government and the empress, who awarded him a gold medal with diamonds"[2] – which saved neither him nor the Sich from reprisal right after the victory. |

posts.title: Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775) (C0033)

The military encirclement and destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich immediately after a joint war. Catherine II's manifesto of 3 August 1775 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XX, no. 14,354) declared: "the Zaporozhian Sich has been utterly destroyed, with the extirpation for the future of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks"[1][2]. The last kish otaman, Kalnyshevsky, "was arrested and sent to the prison of the Solovetsky monastery"[3], where he spent more than 25 years. Hrushevsky describes the mechanics of the treachery: the government "went about the affair slowly, in secret, to catch the Zaporozhians entirely unprepared," and general Tekeli "entered the Zaporozhian lands as a good friend" - then suddenly laid siege to the Sich. The Zaporozhians were even faulted for their own husbandry: they "were establishing their own tillage and thereby severing their dependence on the Russian state"[4].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The encirclement and forcible seizure of the Sich by imperial troops right after the Cossacks had helped the empire win the war. The manifesto records the operation matter-of-factly: "On June 4, Our Lieutenant-General Tekeli, with the troops entrusted to him by us, occupied the Zaporozhian Sich"[1]. |
| **[Destruction of Historical Memory (T0045)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** The issuing of Catherine II's August manifesto, officially erasing the very memory of the Sich: it was destroyed "with the extirpation for the future of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks," for the empire resolved "to destroy the Zaporozhian Sich and the name of the Cossacks derived from it"[1]. Hrushevsky: "The Sich was destroyed, and on 3 August a tsarist decree announced its abolition, 'with the annihilation of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks'"[4]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The arrest and exile of the Sich's top leadership: "In July 1775, after the destruction of the New Sich, by order of Empress Catherine II, Kalnyshevsky was arrested and sent to the prison of the Solovetsky monastery"[3]. Kalnyshevsky spent more than 25 years in confinement; formally freed in 1801, he died in the monastery. |

</details>

posts.title: Administrative Dismantling and Enserfment of the Left Bank (1781–1786)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Administrative Dismantling and Enserfment of the Left Bank (1781–1786) (C0034)

The execution of Catherine II's secret instructions for the institutional and cultural assimilation of the land: the liquidation of the regimental order and the introduction of imperial viceroyalties – the Kyiv Viceroyalty was established by the nominal decree to the Senate of September 16, 1781 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XXI, no. 15,228; execution ordered from November)[1][2], "which finally abolished the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy and its regimental-sotnia administrative-political and military order"[3]; the secularization of monastery lands in 1786 and the legal binding of peasants by Catherine II's decree of May 3, 1783: "each of the villagers is to remain in the place and station where he is registered by the current last revision"[4].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The abolition of the Cossack regimental order and the division of the Left Bank into imperial viceroyalties: the Kyiv Viceroyalty was established by the nominal decree to the Senate of September 16, 1781[1][2], "which finally abolished the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy and its regimental-sotnia administrative-political and military order"[3]; the same decree established the Chernihiv and Novhorod-Siverskyi viceroyalties. |
| **[Legal Segregation of the Population (T0032)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/339):** The legal enserfment of Ukrainian peasants by Catherine II's decree of May 3, 1783, depriving them of the right of free movement: "For the certain and reliable collection of treasury revenues in the viceroyalties of Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Novhorod-Siverskyi and for the prevention of any flights… each of the villagers is to remain in the place and station where he is registered by the current last revision"[4]. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** The secularization and confiscation into the imperial treasury of the lands of Ukrainian Orthodox monasteries: "in 1786, during the secularization, the monastery was closed, and its property and lands passed to the state treasury"[5] – the fate of the Sviatohirsk monastery is typical of the entire 1786 campaign, which deprived the local church of its economic base. |

</details>

posts.title: Military Annexation of the Crimean Khanate (1783)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Military Annexation of the Crimean Khanate (1783) (C0035)

The seizure of the Crimean Khanate and its forcible incorporation into the Russian Empire: "WE have resolved to take under OUR dominion the Crimean peninsula, the island of Taman, and the entire Kuban side"[1]. With regard to Ukraine, the annexation was secured through the forced mobilization of Cossacks as a military resource, the colonization of the adjacent southern steppes to create a loyal rear, and the erasure of Cossack toponyms: the lands of the destroyed Sich were assigned by Catherine II's manifesto of 3 August 1775 "as convenient to the Novorossiysk Governorate"[2]. For Crimea this meant the liquidation of the state and its ruling dynasty: "in the spring of 1782 Khan Shahin Girey was forced to flee under Russian protection"[3], the manifesto on the taking of Crimea was signed by Catherine II on April 8, 1783 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XXI, no. 15,108)[4], and the khan was exiled to Kaluga; the indigenous population was being squeezed out in waves of emigration - "if before 1787 only 8 thousand had emigrated, by 1792 it was already tens of thousands"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Forced Mobilization (T0049)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The use of Ukrainian Cossacks as a military resource for storming Turkish fortresses and consolidating imperial claims to Crimea: at Ochakiv "the 'loyal Cossacks' took part in the storming of the fortress"[5], and in the storming of Izmail "in total over 6 thousand Black Sea Cossacks took part in the battle"[6]. |
| **[Migratory Replacement (T0117.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/389):** The colonization of the steppes adjacent to Crimea with settlers to create a loyal rear: as early as 1752, New Serbia was formed from Serbs – "officially – to guard the southern frontiers from Tatar and Turkish raids, but in fact – to subdue the Zaporozhians"[7], and in 1776 Potemkin directly ordered "not to return fugitives"[8], accelerating the settlement of the south. |
| **[Erasure and Renaming of Place Names (T0043)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/347):** The erasure of the historical names of the Cossack southern territories used as a springboard for the annexation of Crimea: Catherine II's manifesto of 3 August 1775 extirpated "the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks" and poured their lands into an imperial construct – "assigning them as convenient to the Novorossiysk Governorate"[2]. |

</details>

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Establishment of the "Pale of Settlement" (1791) (C0036)

The introduction of discriminatory legislation that territorially restricted the rights of the Jewish population: decree No. 17,006 of December 23, 1791 confirmed the ban on Jews enrolling in the merchantry in the internal Russian cities and ports, extending the rights of citizenship and burgher status only to the Ekaterinoslav Viceroyalty and the Tauride region[1]. From the totality of such acts emerged the Pale of Settlement, running predominantly through colonized Ukrainian territories.

---

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Legal Segregation of the Population (T0032)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/339):** The introduction of territorial discrimination: by the decree of 1791, the Jewish population's right to burgher and merchant status was confined to specific viceroyalties – Ekaterinoslav and Taurida[1] – the legal foundation of the future Pale of Settlement, which confined the area of residence and economic activity to the colonized governorates. |

</details>

# Campaign: Second and Third Partitions of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (1793–1795) (C0037)

The Russian Empire's collusion with the Hohenzollern and Habsburg monarchies to dismember a neighboring state. Under the second partition, "Russia received the central part of Belarus, the Kyiv, Bratslav, and Podillia voivodeships, and the eastern half of the Volhynian voivodeship – in total 250 thousand km2 and over 3 million inhabitants," and after the third, "the Polish state ceased to exist"[1].

| Procedures Carried Out |

| **[Annexation of Territories (T0017)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/325):** The seizure and incorporation into the empire of Right-Bank Ukraine, Volhynia, and Podillia: Russia received "the Kyiv, Bratslav, and Podillia voivodeships and the eastern half of the Volhynian voivodeship," and under the third partition – "the western part of the Volhynian voivodeship, the western parts of the Kholm land and the Belz voivodeship"[1]. |
