posts.title: Creation of the Little Russian Governorate-General (1801–1811)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Creation of the Little Russian Governorate-General (1801–1811) (C0038)

Administrative absorption: "the LITTLE RUSSIAN GOVERNORATE-GENERAL – an administrative-territorial and political unit of the Russian Empire, created in 1802 for the incorporation and integration of Left-Bank Ukraine into the Russian Empire"[1]. The outcome is recorded there as well: "During the existence of the governorate-general, the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy were finally liquidated"[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The erasure of historical borders and the introduction of the imperial vertical: "The governor-general concentrated the entire fullness of administrative power: he was endowed with the right of legislative initiative, determined the degree to which all-Russian laws extended within the governorate-general, and controlled the activity of state institutions, including judicial ones"[1]. |
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** In 1804-1811 the Russian Empire erected a cast-iron Monument of Glory in the center of Poltava in memory of its victory over the army of Charles XII on 27 June 1709 - with the city's own money and to a design sent from St. Petersburg. By the imperial decree to the Senate of 11 September 1804, "On leaving the villages formerly owned by the city of Poltava under state administration and on releasing the income collected from them to the local Governor-General for the erection in Poltava of a monument in memory of 27 June 1709," the city's revenues were assigned to the monument: "the community of Poltava citizens, through a petition submitted to Governor-General Prince Kurakin, has designated all these revenues for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of the day unforgettable for Russia, 27 June 1709, and so we command: the revenues now due for payment, as well as those henceforth collected in favor of this city, shall be released to the local Governor-General until the monument that has been begun is completely finished"[2]. By a second act, the imperial rescript of 9 May 1805 to the Governor-General of Little Russia, "On the erection of a monument in commemoration of the victory won at Poltava by Emperor Peter the Great," the emperor sent a ready-made design and ordered construction to begin: "I forward to you herewith the plans for this monument, drawn up here, charging you... to proceed with its erection on site, except for the bronze ornaments belonging to it, which will be made separately here and delivered to their destination"[2]. That is, Poltava pays, while Petersburg decides what the sign on its land will look like - down to the bronze, which is cast there and shipped ready-made. The monument was founded on 27 June 1804, the cast-iron column was raised in May 1809 under the direction of Moskvin, an engineer of the Luhansk works, and the whole ensemble was opened on 27 June 1811, for the next anniversary of the battle[3][4]. On the medallion of the upper square of the pedestal, inside a serpent ring between two quivers, stood "June the 27th, 1709," and on the opposite side - "Finished in 1809"[3]: the date of someone else's victory was made into the date of the place itself. Both inscriptions, together with the bronze bas-reliefs, disappeared in 1901 - the pre-revolutionary survey records it tersely: "This inscription and the preceding one were destroyed in 1901, and at the same time the bronze bas-reliefs that surrounded them were taken by persons unknown"[3]; they were restored only during the capital repairs of 1953[4]. The monument still stands in Poltava: as of August 2026 it is listed as a monument of national significance under heritage protection number 160010-Н[5], the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance recommended dismantling it in a letter of 29 July 2024[6], but decisions on monuments of national significance are made by the government, and the list of such decisions as of 20 May 2026 does not include the monument[7]. |

</details>

# Campaign: War with Napoleon: Forced Mobilization and Deception (1812) (C0040)

The authorities' false promise to return the lost Cossack liberties to the indigenous population in exchange for blood. The empire squeezed the maximum out of the land: "on both of its banks, Ukraine was used for the recruitment, equipping, and movement of troops… including a 75-thousand-strong militia from the Kyiv, Podillia, Chernihiv, and Poltava governorates"[1], and after the war the formations were disbanded and the promises forgotten[2]; when the Buh Cossacks refused to be turned into military settlers in 1817, their uprising was crushed by four regiments with artillery[1].

---

posts.title: Introduction of Military Settlements and Liquidation of the Danubian Sich (1817–1828)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Introduction of Military Settlements and Liquidation of the Danubian Sich (1817–1828) (C0041)

A campaign to turn the free population into rightless military settlers. "The trigger was the order abolishing the Buh Cossack Host and turning the Cossacks into military settlers"[1] – the Buh Cossacks' uprising of 1817 was brutally suppressed. There were two acts, on opposite sides of the uprising: the nominal decree of April 17, 1817 transferred the Buh Host's district "into direct military administration" (PSZRI, vol. XXXIV, no. 26,802) - this was the trigger; the decree of October 8, 1817 (no. 27,081), issued after the suppression, formalized the liquidation: "the name of the Buh Cossack Host is abolished"[2]. Later, kish otaman Hladky with part of the Danubian Cossacks "on May 30 (18), 1828 crossed the Kiliya mouth of the Danube, entered the port of Izmail, and joined the Russian army"[3] – this was the end of the last free host: the Danubian Sich "existed from the last quarter of the 18th century until 1828"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The transfer of Cossacks to the status of rightless military settlers (the Arakcheev system), which provoked the uprising of 1817: "The trigger was the order abolishing the Buh Cossack Host and turning the Cossacks into military settlers… The reprisal against the rebellious Cossacks was extraordinarily brutal: many were cut down with sabers, drowned in the Southern Buh, flogged to death"[1]. There were two acts, on opposite sides of the uprising: the nominal decree of April 17, 1817 transferred the Buh Host's district "into direct military administration" - this was the trigger; the decree of October 8, 1817, issued after the suppression, formalized the liquidation: "the name of the Buh Cossack Host is abolished"[2]. |
| **[Bribery of Elites (T0015)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/324):** The luring of kish otaman Hladky over to the empire's side in 1828: part of the Danubians "headed by kish otaman Y. Hladky, on May 30 (18), 1828, crossed the Kiliya mouth of the Danube, entered the port of Izmail, and joined the Russian army"[3]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The otaman's defection left the Cossacks remaining beyond the Danube exposed to the Porte's retaliation and put an end to the last free Cossack host: the Danubian Sich "existed from the last quarter of the 18th century until 1828"[3]. |

</details>

# Campaign: Ban on Ukrainian Book Printing (1720) (C0043)

A campaign to introduce censorship and institutional linguistic assimilation. Peter I's decree of October 5, 1720 banned the printing of books in the indigenous people's language at the key printing houses: "In the Kyiv-Pechersk and Chernihiv printing houses no new books whatsoever are to be printed except previous church editions, and even those old church books are to be corrected before printing for complete conformity with the Great Russian church books, so that there be no discord or distinct dialect in them"[1].

| **[Legislative Ban on the Native Language (T0113.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** The ruler's direct decree against the very language of the local population in print: the same decree of Peter I ordered books to be checked against Muscovite ones, "so that there be no discord or distinct dialect in them"[1]. |

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Russification of Education and Religion (1769–1786) (C0044)

A systematic campaign of the Russian Empire to root out the indigenous people's language from education and religion: "in 1769 the Holy Synod not only refused permission to print South Russian primers, but ordered the confiscation of those already in people's hands"[1]; by an order of 26 October 1784, the Kyiv metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky directed the rector and prefect of the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy "to take unremitting care of the unfailing and unomitted observance, by teachers and students alike, of the rules of Russian orthography," under the threat of expelling students from the clerical estate[2]; in 1786 the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy was prescribed the empire-wide mode of instruction[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Legislative Ban on the Native Language (T0113.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** The mass confiscation of national educational and religious literature: "in 1769 the Holy Synod not only refused permission to print South Russian primers, but ordered the confiscation of those already in people's hands, since the primers of that time were regarded as church books"[1]. |
| **[Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language (T0114.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/379):** The Russification of teaching in the country's principal institution of learning: from 1784 metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky introduced new classes of geography and history at the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy with an order to conduct them "in pure Russian," and by his order of 26 October 1784 demanded that teachers and students observe "the rules of orthography proper to the Russian language" - teachers faced dismissal for lapses, and students expulsion from the clerical estate[2]. The unification was completed by the order of February 13, 1786: "to adopt immediately for the Kyiv Academy the mode of instruction legalized for all schools in the All-Russian Empire"[3] – the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy was transferred to the empire-wide mode of teaching. |
| **[Ban on Worship in the Native Language (T0116.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/387):** The displacement of the local population's language from the sacred sphere: metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky's order of 26 October 1784 demanded that students and future priests practice "the reading of church books of every kind, and above all the Bible, acquiring a good and pure pronunciation" - after the Moscow model instead of the Ukrainian church tradition, under the threat of expulsion from the clerical estate[2], and in 1786 metropolitan Myslavsky prescribed to the clergy the unification of pronunciation and orthography along the Russian model[3]. |

</details>

# Campaign: Abolition of Magdeburg Rights (1831) (C0045)

The abolition of the traditional system of municipal self-government: "The final liquidation of Magdeburg law on the western Ukrainian lands took place in 1786, and in the cities of Central and Left-Bank Ukraine – in 1831 (in Kyiv – 1834)"[1] – the final stage of embedding the cities into the imperial administrative-judicial system, begun as early as the reforms of the 1780s.

| **[Exclusion of the Native Language from Official Use (T0113.002)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/375):** The displacement of the native language from the official sphere of the cities: with the liquidation of the remnants of Magdeburg self-government, the last institutional support for the local legal tradition disappeared – Ukrainian-language court proceedings had been curtailed as early as the extension of the all-Russian judicial system in the 1780s[1]. |

posts.title: The Valuev Circular: Ban on the Language and Schools (1862–1869)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Valuev Circular: Ban on the Language and Schools (1862–1869) (C0046)

A state campaign to destroy the Ukrainian language and culture: in 1862 the authorities closed the Sunday schools that taught in Ukrainian - "for the alleged presence of revolutionary propaganda"[1], the ban on the national press, the official denial of the language's existence – the Valuev circular: "there was not, is not, and cannot be any distinct Little Russian language"[2] – and bonuses to officials "in the ten South-Western governorates for persons of Russian origin, excluding, however, local natives," fixed by the decrees of 1869 and 1886[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (5)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Destruction of Local Knowledge Systems (T0044)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/348):** The liquidation of education in the native language: in 1859–1862 the intelligentsia and students founded 111 Sunday schools in Ukraine to teach adults literacy, with instruction conducted in Ukrainian; in 1862 the authorities closed these schools "for the alleged presence of revolutionary propaganda"[1]. |
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** The closure of the national press: the Ukrainian socio-political and literary journal "Osnova" (St. Petersburg, January 1861 - October 1862) came to an end: the plans to reorganize the publication were thwarted by the minister of internal affairs Valuev, who refused to sanction its publication under a renewed program[1]. |
| **[Legislative Ban on the Native Language (T0113.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** Valuev's secret circular to the censorship committees (18 July 1863), which halted printing in the native language: "the clearance of books in the Little Russian language, whether of religious content, educational, or generally intended for the people's elementary reading, is to be suspended"[2]. |
| **[Denial of a Distinct Identity (T0010)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The official refusal to recognize the language and identity – the formula of Valuev's circular (1863): "there was not, is not, and cannot be any distinct Little Russian language, and their dialect, used by the common folk, is the same Russian language, only spoiled by Poland's influence upon it"[2]. |
| **[Financial Incentives for Assimilators (T0130)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/402):** The introduction of bonuses for the policy of denationalization: by decrees of the tsarist administration of 1869 and 1886, officials "in the ten South-Western governorates - persons of Russian origin, excluding, however, local natives" - were assigned bonuses for successes in the Russification of Ukraine[3] - part of the authorities' systematic plans to strengthen the "Russian assimilatory potential" of the Western krai after the Polish uprising of 1863, which included material benefits for Russian officials and teachers[4]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

posts.title: The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Ems Ukaz and Total Censorship (1876–1887) (C0047)

The complete displacement of the language from the cultural and literary sphere. The Ems ukase prescribed: "Not to permit the import into the empire… of any books whatsoever published abroad in the Little Russian dialect," "To forbid in the empire the printing, in the same dialect, of any original works or translations whatsoever," and "To forbid likewise any stage performances, texts to musical scores, and public readings in the same dialect"[1]. The permitted dictionaries were allowed only "on condition of their being printed in conformity with all-Russian orthography"[2].

Five years later the rules were revised by a Special Conference - it included Solsky, Ostrovsky, the chief procurator of the Synod Pobedonostsev, and Viazemsky, - and the minister of internal affairs Ignatiev reported the result to the emperor on 3 October 1881; assent followed on 8 October[3]. There were no plans to publish the revision, and Ignatiev explained why: "the rules on the use of the Little Russian dialect established in 1876 were not promulgated, and therefore it is not intended to make the projected clarifications known to the general public"[3]. The circular went out to governor-general Drenteln on 16 October stamped "Confidential"[3] - that is, people were judged by rules they were never shown.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (5)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Legislative Ban on the Native Language (T0113.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** A total legislative ban on the language: "Not to permit the import into the empire… of any books whatsoever published abroad in the Little Russian dialect"; "To forbid likewise any stage performances, texts to musical scores, and public readings in the same dialect"[1]. |
| **[Replacement of the Native Language's Alphabet (T0115.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/381):** A concession that was in fact a choice between two alien orthographies: the 1881 revision allowed dictionaries to be printed, but "on condition of their being printed in conformity with all-Russian orthography, or with the orthography used in Little Russia no later than the 18th century"[3]. That is, either the metropole's orthography or an archaic one was admissible - contemporary Ukrainian orthography was not allowed in any form. The same document permitted stage texts to musical scores to be printed only "on condition of generally accepted Russian orthography," and made Ukrainian-language performances dependent on administrative permission: "dramatic plays, scenes and couplets in the Little Russian dialect... may be performed on stage, each time, however, with the special permission of the governors-general, and in localities not subordinate to governors-general - with the permission of the governors"[3]. |
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** The censor's refusal to consider national manuscripts: "On a Ukrainian grammar prepared in Russian, the censor wrote the resolution: 'It would be naive to hope for permission to print the grammar of a language that must not exist'"[2]. |
| **[Denial of a Distinct Identity (T0010)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The ideological justification of the censorship refusal – the language was declared nonexistent by definition: the censor's resolution about "the grammar of a language that must not exist"[2]. |
| **[Liquidation of National Civic Organizations (T0128)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The theater was banned not as repertoire but as an institution: the third point of the 1881 revision prescribed "to completely forbid the establishment of a specifically Little Russian theater and the formation of troupes for performing plays and scenes exclusively in the Little Russian dialect"[3]. Individual plays remained permissible - with administrative permission for each staging. The ban struck not at the text but at the very possibility of a permanent company existing: performing occasionally was allowed, being a Ukrainian theater was not. The report with this point was submitted by the minister of internal affairs Ignatiev; the emperor's assent followed on 8 October 1881[3]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

1. Александр II / Особое совещание (18.05.1876). (1876). Эмский указ.
2. Василь Лизанчук. (1995). Навічно кували кайдани.
3. Відп. ред. Г. Боряк; упоряд. Г. Боряк, В. Баран, Л. Гісцова, Л. Демченко, О. Музичук, П. Найденко, В. Шандра; НАН України, Ін-т історії України; Укрдержархів, ЦДІАК України. (2013). Українська ідентичність і мовне питання в Російській імперії.

posts.title: Ban on the Language in Books and Public Speeches (1892–1905)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Ban on the Language in Books and Public Speeches (1892–1905) (C0049)

A state campaign to drive the language out of public space and literature: in 1892 the Main Administration for Press Affairs directed the censorship committee to suppress translations into Ukrainian, "reducing the number of such talentless works for purely state purposes"[1]; at the archaeological congress in Kyiv in 1899, scholars from Austrian-ruled Ukraine were forbidden to read papers in Ukrainian - in protest they withdrew from participation[2]; at the unveiling of the Kotliarevsky monument in Poltava on 30-31 August 1903, only guests from Galicia were allowed to speak Ukrainian, while the mayor forbade the locals to do so, citing an order of the ministry of internal affairs[2]. Even children's literature fell under the ban: the 1895 circular prohibited Ukrainian books "for children's reading"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Legislative Ban on the Native Language (T0113.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** The ban on the language in public speech: at the archaeological congress in Kyiv in 1899 the authorities forbade scholars from Austrian-ruled Ukraine to read papers in Ukrainian - they demonstratively withdrew from the sessions[2]. At the unveiling of the Kotliarevsky monument in Poltava on 30-31 August 1903, the Galicians were allowed to speak Ukrainian, but when local Ukrainians began reading a greeting address, the mayor cut the reading short, citing an order of the ministry of internal affairs; only in 1906 did the Senate revoke the ban, even reprimanding the minister for "the impropriety of his actions"[2]. In 1904-1905 the commissions of the Kyiv and Kharkiv universities and the Academy of Sciences, consulted by the Committee of Ministers, spoke out for lifting the bans on the Ukrainian word, yet the decrees of 1876 and 1881 were never formally revoked[2]. |
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** Total censorship of translations and book imports: in 1892 the Main Administration for Press Affairs directed the censorship committee to suppress translations into Ukrainian, "reducing the number of such talentless works for purely state purposes"[1]; "The ban on importing Ukrainian books from abroad was confirmed in the harshest form in 1894"[3]. |
| **[Destruction of Local Knowledge Systems (T0044)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/348):** The destruction of the basis for teaching children in their native language: "By a special circular of the Main Administration for Press Affairs in 1895, the printing of any books or collections in the Ukrainian language for children's reading was forbidden, 'even if in the substance of their content they appeared well-intentioned.'" The censor's resolution on a children's collection: "Obviously written for children, but they must learn in Russian. — Forbid"[3]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

2. Юрій Шевельов. (1987). Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус.
3. Василь Лизанчук. (1995). Навічно кували кайдани.

posts.title: Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910) (C0050)

A campaign to suppress the legal civic activity of the indigenous people: in the Poltava and Kharkiv regions the "Prosvita" societies were banned from their very founding, and in 1908–1910, under Stolypin, virtually all "Prosvitas" were closed, except the branches of the Katerynoslav governorate[1]. Justifying the crackdown, Stolypin declared in an address to the Senate that the revival of Ukrainian cultural life was undesirable, for "the three principal branches of Eastern Slavdom, both by origin and by language, cannot but constitute one whole"[1]. Stolypin's circular of 1910 classed Ukrainians among the "aliens" and prescribed "to refuse without fail the registration" of their societies[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Liquidation of National Civic Organizations (T0128)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The direct closure of legal educational societies: of the roughly forty "Prosvitas" of Russian-ruled Ukraine, those in the Poltava and Kharkiv regions were banned from their very founding, and in 1908–1910, under Stolypin, virtually all the rest were liquidated, except the branches of the Katerynoslav governorate[1]. The crackdown received its doctrinal grounding: Stolypin declared in an address to the Senate that the revival of Ukrainian cultural life was undesirable, for "the three principal branches of Eastern Slavdom, both by origin and by language, cannot but constitute one whole"[1]. Stolypin's circular to the governors (20 January 1910) — a complete ban on self-organization: "when considering petitions for the registration of any alien societies whatsoever… one must… refuse without fail the registration of their charters"[2]. |
| **[Legal Segregation of the Population (T0032)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/339):** The official classing of the indigenous population as aliens: Stolypin prescribed to the governors to refuse the registration of "any alien societies whatsoever, including Ukrainian and Jewish ones, regardless of the aims they pursue"[2]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

1. Юрій Шевельов. (1987). Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус.

posts.title: Ban on Culture and the Press Before World War I (1913–1914)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Ban on Culture and the Press Before World War I (1913–1914) (C0051)

The Russian Empire continued destroying the indigenous people's culture on the eve of the war: the curator of the Kyiv school district, Derevytsky, in 1913 "issued an instruction in which he declared students' attendance of Ukrainian theatrical performances as inadmissible as spending time in billiard halls or beer houses, and in 1914 categorically forbade all educational institutions of the Kyiv district to mark the 100th jubilee of Taras Shevchenko"[1]; with the outbreak of the war, Nicholas II by a personal decree of 20 July 1914 introduced military censorship with the command's right "to suspend periodical publications"[2] - and that very day the military authorities of the Kyiv military district closed the only Ukrainian daily newspaper, "Rada"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Cultural Chauvinism (T0115.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/383):** The ban on attending cultural events: the district curator "issued an instruction in which he declared students' attendance of Ukrainian theatrical performances as inadmissible as spending time in billiard halls or beer houses"[1]. |
| **[Destruction of Historical Memory (T0045)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** The erasure of the memory of national heroes: "In January 1914, minister of internal affairs Nikolai Maklakov signed a circular by which he forbade throughout all governorates of the empire 'public celebrations of the Little Russian writer Taras Shevchenko'"[4]. |
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** The purge of the information space: Nicholas II's personal decree of 20 July 1914 on military censorship gave the command the right "to forbid for a set term, by their own authority and within the locality subordinate to them, any assemblies whatsoever, and to suspend periodical publications, as well as the transmission of postal items and telegrams"[2]. On this basis the military administration of the Kyiv military district that very day closed the only Ukrainian daily newspaper, "Rada," and confiscated at the printing house the print runs of "Svitlo" and of the "Literary-Scientific Herald," and on 9 January 1915 all Ukrainian periodicals were shut down[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Stalinist Terror and the End of Ukrainization (1922–1939)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Stalinist Terror and the End of Ukrainization (1922–1939) (C0052)

The suppression of the national revival in the USSR: the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the Council of People's Commissars of 14 December 1932, signed by Stalin and Molotov, declared that "Ukrainization was carried out mechanically" and ordered "to immediately transfer in the North Caucasus the record-keeping of the soviet and cooperative bodies of the 'Ukrainized' districts, as well as all published newspapers and journals, from the Ukrainian language to Russian"[1]; the annihilation of most Ukrainian writers of the 1920s-1930s went down in history as the "Executed Renaissance"[2]; the resolution of the USSR Council of People's Commissars and the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 13 March 1938 No. 324 ordered "to introduce the teaching of the Russian language as a subject of study in the schools of the national republics and regions from September 1, 1938"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Extermination Based on Identity (T0120)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/392):** The targeted physical annihilation of the national cultural elite. The official turn was sealed by the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the Council of People's Commissars "On Grain Procurements in Ukraine, the North Caucasus, and the Western Region" of 14 December 1932, signed by Stalin and Molotov: Ukrainization was declared to have been carried out "mechanically," which, in the resolution's own words, "made it easier for bourgeois-nationalist elements, Petliurites and the like to create their legal covers, their counter-revolutionary cells and organizations"[1]. The term "Executed Renaissance" denotes precisely "the repressive policy of communist Moscow aimed at the physical destruction of the Ukrainian intellectual elite of the 1920s–30s (more broadly – of the entire nationally conscious Ukrainian intelligentsia) and the tabooing of its creative achievements"[2]. |
| **[Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality (T0114.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/377):** The compulsory introduction of the metropole's language into schools: the resolution of the USSR Council of People's Commissars and the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 13 March 1938 No. 324 "On the Compulsory Study of the Russian Language in the Schools of the National Republics and Regions" ordered "to introduce the teaching of the Russian language as a subject of study in the schools of the national republics and regions from September 1, 1938" - from the 2nd grade in all non-Russian primary schools and from the 3rd grade in incomplete secondary and secondary schools[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Creation of a Single "Soviet People" (1958–1970)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Creation of a Single "Soviet People" (1958–1970) (C0053)

The USSR's official campaign to erase national distinctions: The start was given by the USSR Law "On Strengthening the Connection of School with Life and on the Further Development of the System of Public Education in the USSR" of December 24, 1958: it contained no direct norm on language, leaving the matter to the republics[1]; the republican Law of the Ukrainian SSR of April 17, 1959, by its Article 9, made the choice of the language of instruction a matter for parents[2]. The Third Program of the CPSU, adopted by the 22nd Congress in October 1961, proclaimed "a new stage in the development of national relations in the USSR, characterized by the further drawing together of nations and the achievement of their complete unity" - up to and including "the effacement of national distinctions, especially of language distinctions"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality (T0114.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/377):** The legislative transfer of schools through "freedom of choice": the union Law of December 24, 1958 left the language of instruction to the republics[1], and the Law of the Ukrainian SSR of April 17, 1959 wrote into Article 9: "Instruction in the schools of the Ukrainian SSR is conducted in the pupils' native language. It is for the parents to decide to which school, with which language of instruction, to send their children" - the study of a language not taught in a given school became optional[2]. |
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** The material sign of the "merging of nations" was erected in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, the city of the Pereiaslav Rada: "on 8 October 1961, a majestic monument in honor of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia was unveiled on B. Khmelnytsky Square"[4]. The authorities unveiled the sign themselves: according to the newsreel Radianska Ukraina No. 49, the opening rally was addressed by Petro Shelest, first secretary of the Kyiv obkom of the CPU, and Pankratov, a secretary of the Moscow obkom of the party - the metropole spoke at the unveiling in its own voice[5]. The composition consisted of two female figures representing Ukraine and Russia and three bas-reliefs with medallions: "a torch, 1654; a hammer and sickle in the rays of the sun, 1917; the Order of Victory, 1945"[6]. The sign's purpose is recorded in its own protection passport: "The monument is a symbol of the eternal, unbreakable friendship and the indestructible monolithic unity of the fraternal peoples - Ukrainian and Russian…"[7]. Four years after the unveiling, the sign was taken under state protection by the resolution of the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR of 21 July 1965 No. 711 "On the approval of the list of monuments of art, history and archaeology of the Ukrainian SSR"[8][9]. The pedestal bore the inscription "Forever together - forever with the Russian people"; in early December 2021 it was removed by unknown persons[10], and the monument itself was dismantled on 7 July 2022 - by an order of the Ministry of Culture that struck the monument, protection No. 5894-Ko, off the register "due to the loss of the subject of protection"[11]. |

</details>

posts.title: Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Financial Russification of Schools (1978–1983) (C0054)

The Soviet Union introduced a system of direct material incentives for assimilation: pursuant to the resolution of the USSR Council of Ministers of 13 October 1978 No. 835 "On measures for the further improvement of the study and teaching of the Russian language in the union republics," the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR, by its resolution of 2 November 1978 No. 518, introduced the study of Russian from the first grades of Ukrainian schools starting with the 1980/81 school year[1]; the all-Union conference "The Russian Language — the Language of Friendship and Cooperation of the Peoples of the USSR" (Tashkent, 22–24 May 1979) spelled out Russification measures down to kindergartens[2]; the resolution of the CPSU Central Committee and the USSR Council of Ministers of 26 May 1983 No. 473 "On additional measures for improving the study of the Russian language in general-education schools and other educational institutions of the union republics" and the resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Ukraine and the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR of 10 June 1983 raised the salary rates of Russian-language teachers by 15 percent from 1984[2][3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Imposition of Asymmetric Bilingualism and Optionality (T0114.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/377):** Administrative pressure on schools: pursuant to the resolution of the USSR Council of Ministers of 13 October 1978 No. 835, the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR, by its resolution of 2 November 1978 No. 518, obliged the ministry of education of the Ukrainian SSR to introduce, from the 1980/81 school year, the study of the Russian language in the first grades of general-education schools with Ukrainian as the language of instruction[1]. |
| **[Cultural Chauvinism (T0115.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/383):** The ideological exaltation of the metropole's language: the all-Union scientific-theoretical conference "The Russian Language — the Language of Friendship and Cooperation of the Peoples of the USSR" adopted detailed recommendations on Russification - from organizing "the study of the Russian language in the senior groups of preschool institutions" to "the use of the Russian language in lessons in other school subjects" in the senior grades of national schools[2]. |
| **[Financial Discrimination Against Teachers (T0114.002)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/378):** Financial privileges for teaching in the metropole's language: pursuant to the resolution of the CPSU Central Committee and the USSR Council of Ministers of 26 May 1983 No. 473 "On additional measures for improving the study of the Russian language in general-education schools and other educational institutions of the union republics," the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Ukraine and the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR, by a resolution of 10 June 1983 - signed by Shcherbytsky and Liashko, stamped "Not for the press" - raised from 1984 by 15 percent the salary rates of teachers of Russian language and literature and allowed classes of more than 25 pupils to be split into subgroups for Russian lessons[2][3]. |

</details>

# Campaign: Suppression of the Shebelynka Uprising (1829) (C0056)

The forcible suppression of a mass anti-serfdom uprising in Sloboda Ukraine that broke out within the system of military settlements: "The servile condition of the military settlements' inhabitants caused the Buh Cossacks' uprising of 1817, the Chuhuiv uprising of 1819, the Shebelynka uprising of 1829, and others"[1]. The scale is recorded by the EHU: "Up to 3 thousand peasants gathered in Shebelynka," and "on May 30, 1829 a bloody reprisal against the defiant began, during which 109 people died"[2].

The Russian Empire's regular army suppresses a national liberation uprising: the insurgent detachments in Volhynia, the Zhytomyr region, Podillia, and the Kyiv region "were routed by the tsarist troops in April–May 1831," after which "the tsarist government resorted to brutal repressions against the participants of the uprising"[1]. # Campaign: Liquidation of the Greek Catholic Church (1839) (C0059)

Institutional seizure and spiritual unification: the empire liquidates the independent Uniate church on the Right Bank, transferring the flock and property under the control of the state church. The mechanism is recorded in the fates of monasteries: "in connection with the tsarist regime's liquidation of the Union in this region (1839), the monastery was closed, and its buildings destroyed"[1]; "By the mid-19th century all monasteries of the Basilian order on the territory of the Russian Empire had been liquidated"[2].

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|

| **[Forced Conversion to the Metropole's Religion (T0116.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/385):** The forced transfer of the Uniate faithful of the Right Bank into the empire's state church (the Holy Synod; the patriarchate in Russia was abolished until 1917) for the spiritual assimilation of the population: the Basilian monasteries – the mainstay of the Union – were liquidated throughout the empire by the mid-19th century[2]. |

posts.title: Crushing of the Cyril and Methodius Society (1847)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Crushing of the Cyril and Methodius Society (1847) (C0060)

The secret police's blow against the intellectual elite of the indigenous people: "In March 1847 the society was crushed by the gendarmes. The police managed to identify 12 members of the clandestine organization… The tsarist authorities judged the society's program documents a serious threat to the foundations of autocracy"[1]. The sentences for all the accused were proposed by the chief of gendarmes Orlov in his report to the emperor of May 26, 1847, on which Nicholas I inscribed "Execute"[2]. It was accompanied by trials, exiles, and Shevchenko's dispatch into the army "with the institution over the poet of 'the strictest surveillance with a prohibition on writing and drawing'"[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Liquidation of National Civic Organizations (T0128)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The destruction of the first political organization of the Ukrainian intelligentsia following student Petrov's denunciation to the secret police: "In March 1847 the society was crushed by the gendarmes. The police managed to identify 12 members of the clandestine organization"[1]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Arrests, interrogations – the gendarmes "resorted to brutal pressure" and "applied refined methods of psychological processing"[1], and reprisal against the leaders: the sentences were set out in the report of the chief of gendarmes Orlov to the emperor of May 26, 1847, with Nicholas I's resolution "Execute"[2]. Shevchenko was sent into the army "with the institution over the poet of 'the strictest surveillance with a prohibition on writing and drawing'"[3][2]. Hrushevsky: the brotherhood "was seized while still in the midst of its very formation" after a student's denunciation; "The heaviest punishment fell on Shevchenko: he was given over to the soldiery and exiled to the trans-Caspian desert, forbidden to write and to paint," and "persecutions and prohibitions previously unheard of descended upon Ukrainian thought and the Ukrainian word… the very words Ukraine, Little Russia, Hetmanate were deemed criminal"[4]. The brotherhood's co-founder Mykola Hulak "was imprisoned in the Shlisselburg fortress (1847-50), then exiled to Perm under strict police surveillance (1850-59)"[5]. |

</details>

A grueling geopolitical war of the empire, accompanied by the mass mobilization of the Ukrainian peasantry. Nicholas I's manifesto on the state militia and the decrees on its levy of 29 January 1855 (Nos. 28.991–28.993) gave rise to hopes of freedom - even though the Kyiv governorate was not on the list of governorates called up at all[1]: "the movement for re-Cossackization in March–April engulfed over 500 villages and towns in 8 of the 12 districts of the Kyiv governorate… To suppress the 'Cossack movement' the government threw in regular troops and police"[2].

posts.title: Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876) (C0063)

Against the backdrop of large-scale territorial conquests, the empire conceptualizes its superiority over the colonized peoples. The ideologue Katkov formulates: "to recognize some element as a distinct nation does not mean granting it freedom, but giving it power, endowing it with binding force. In the recognition of a nation the question of power, of government, of the state is decided"[1] – the recognition of Ukrainians as a nation was ruled out as a question of power.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Cultivation of a Logic of Superiority (T0003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/313):** The systematic imposition of the metropole's logic of superiority. Researchers reconstruct Katkov's logic thus: "a nation must be a tribe capable of creating a state; only a state nation can establish order in a given territory; tribes incapable of creating a state have to submit to the state nation"[1]. Katkov himself wrote: "In the recognition of a nation the question of power, of government, of the state is decided"[1]. Hrushevsky records both the thesis and its reach: Valuev invoked an imaginary "majority of Little Russians" who allegedly "know neither a Ukrainian nationality nor language, only one Russian people and tongue," while the ideology's mouthpieces carried it to the formula "there are no Ruthenians — there is only one 'Russian people' from the Carpathians to Kamchatka"[2]. |
| **[Forced Mobilization (T0049)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The use of Ukrainians within the imperial army in large-scale wars of conquest in the Caucasus and Central Asia – recruit conscription had extended to the Ukrainian governorates since the liquidation of the autonomy[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Russo-Turkish War and Pan-Slavism (1877–1878)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Russo-Turkish War and Pan-Slavism (1877–1878) (C0064)

The use of the inhabitants of the Ukrainian governorates in yet another geopolitical war in the Balkans. Imperial expansion was justified by religion and the ideology of Pan-Slavism – Dostoevsky formulated it as a mission: the Slavs "for a long time… will be unable to recognize Russia's selflessness and her great, holy raising, unheard of in the world, of the banner of the greatest idea"[1].

---

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Justification Through Religion (T0024)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/332):** The ideological justification of a war of conquest by religion and Pan-Slavism: per Dostoevsky, "by Russia's insistence and blood the Slavs have already been liberated… the Turkish empire no longer exists and… the Balkan peninsula is free and lives a new life"[1] – the war was given the status of a sacred mission of liberating co-religionists. |
| **[Forced Mobilization (T0049)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The mobilization of the inhabitants of the colonized Ukrainian governorates into the imperial army for the war in the Balkans – under the universal military conscription in force in the Ukrainian lands since the liquidation of the autonomy[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888) (C0065)

In 1888 the Russian Empire erected in central Kyiv a monument to Bohdan Khmelnytsky - a sign of the city's belonging to the empire and of "unity" with Moscow. The pedestal bore programmatic inscriptions: "We will to be under the tsar of the east, the Orthodox one" and "To Bohdan Khmelnytsky – one and indivisible Russia"[1]. The monument was unveiled on 11 July 1888 on Sophia Square; the committee for its construction was headed by Mikhail Yuzefovich - an official of the Kyiv educational district and author of the memorandum that formed the basis of the Ems ukase of 1876[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Rewriting of History (T0004)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** On the pedestal of the Khmelnytsky monument (1888) the empire cast a programmatic statement about the past: on the front side stood the phrase "We will to be under the tsar of the east, the Orthodox one," attributed to the Pereiaslav Rada, and on the right - the imperial formula "To Bohdan Khmelnytsky – one and indivisible Russia"[1]. Brought together, they presented the events of 1654 as a voluntary and final choice in favor of a single Russian state, and the entire history of the Hetmanate as the road to that choice. |
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** On 11 July 1888 the Russian Empire unveiled the Bohdan Khmelnytsky monument on Sophia Square in Kyiv - a sign of "unity" with Moscow: on the left side of the pedestal stood the dates "1654-1888," counting the city's history from the Pereiaslav Rada[1]. The committee for its construction was headed by Mikhail Yuzefovich[1] - an official of the Kyiv educational district and author of the memorandum that formed the basis of the Ems ukase of 1876[2]. The conference convened over that memorandum, sitting with Yuzefovich's participation, resolved "not to permit the import into the empire, without special authorization of the Main Administration for Press Affairs, of any books or brochures whatsoever published abroad in the Little Russian dialect," and "to forbid the printing and publishing in the empire of original works and translations in that dialect, with the sole exceptions of: a) historical documents and monuments and b) works of belles-lettres" - the latter permitted only in Russian orthography and from a manuscript reviewed by the censorship[3]. Under the decree of the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR of 7 May 1919 on removing from squares and streets the monuments erected to tsars and tsarist minions, two of the three inscriptions were knocked off the pedestal; the remaining one was ordered removed by Hrynko, chairman of the Kyiv gubernia executive committee - academician Yefremov recorded this in his diary on 6 February 1925 - and in the end the side plaques were replaced with blank ones, while "Bohdan Khmelnytskyi 1888" was carved on the front stone[1]. |

</details>

# Campaign: Industrial Colonization and Resource Exploitation of the South (1890) (C0066)

At the end of the 19th century, the Russian Empire turns the Ukrainian lands into a raw-materials colony, exploiting the resources of the Donbas and deliberately importing labor: "42 percent of the 425,413 workers counted in the census were born outside Ukraine," and "in 1892, 80 percent of the workforce at the mines and plants of Yuzivka… had arrived from the Moscow region"[1].

|---|
| **[Resource Exploitation (T0102)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/364):** The Ukrainian regions became the empire's main raw-materials donor: "In 1910 coal extraction amounted to 1 billion poods, and in 1913 – 1.5 billion poods. Over this time the Donbas's share in the empire's coal industry grew from 67% to 74%… Before World War I, Ukrainian metallurgy produced 2/3 of the pig iron smelted in the empire"[2]. |

"Among the workers and miners of the Donbas, ethnic Russians from Central Russia predominated… The rural population of the Donbas was mostly ethnically Ukrainian"[3]. |

# Campaign: All-Russian Census and the Erasure of Identity (1897) (C0067)

The empire conducts a general census embedded in the doctrine of the "triune Russian people": official scholarship classified Ukrainian speech as "the Little Russian dialect of the Russian language"[1], not an independent language. "The census of 1897 recorded not nationality but the respondents' native tongue, and since many Ukrainians named Russian as such, there were in fact more ethnic Ukrainians than indicated in the census"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (1)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Denial of a Distinct Identity (T0010)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The denial to Ukrainians of the status of a separate people at the level of official doctrine: imperial scholarship maintained that "The relation of the Little Russian dialect to the Russian language may be likened to the relation between the Slovak dialect and the Czech language… but not to the relation between the Polish, Czech, Serbian, etc. languages, on the one hand, and Russian, on the other"[1] – Ukrainian was considered a dialect, not a language. The census worked as the same instrument for dissolving the nation in imperial statistics: "The census of 1897 recorded not nationality but the respondents' native tongue, and since many Ukrainians named Russian as such, there were in fact more ethnic Ukrainians than indicated in the census"[2]. |

</details>

# Campaign: Black Hundred Terror and Pogroms (1905–1907) (C0068)

The imperial authorities sponsor and cover for radical Russian nationalist organizations for the suppression of the revolution and for terror. The "Union of the Russian People" was "a Black-Hundred organization… The organization received financial support from the state and was patronized by Russian emperor Nicholas II… Mass Jewish pogroms provoked by the 'Union' took place, particularly in Ukraine, in the 'Pale of Settlement'"[1]; of its 400 thousand members, nearly half were in Ukrainian cities[1].

|---|

In 1907 there existed about 800 local branches of the 'Union'"[1]. |

In Odesa, "Low-ranking policemen and soldiers failed to interfere with the pogromists and in many instances participated in the looting and killing"[3], and the commander of the district's troops told policemen: "all of us sympathize in our souls with the pogrom"[3]. |

The outcome was "the mass Jewish pogroms provoked by the 'Union,' particularly in Ukraine, in the 'Pale of Settlement'"[1]. |

# Campaign: Stolypin Repressions and Mass Displacement (1906–1914) (C0069)

The suppression of protests and an agrarian reform that economically squeezed Ukrainian peasants off their native lands: "The resettlement movement gained great momentum, and during 1906–12 about 1 million people left Ukraine for Asiatic Russia… The majority of migrants were landless and land-poor peasants (67%)"[1] – nearly a quarter of the resettlers, failing to take root, returned.

The largest number of resettlers came from Left-Bank Ukraine, whose peasantry suffered from land scarcity"[1]; land and credit were unobtainable at home, while "Low land prices beyond the Urals and encouraging government credits… attracted the poor peasantry and prompted it to migrate"[1] – state coercion was disguised as voluntary resettlement. |

posts.title: Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Failure of the Political Seizure of the UNR in Kyiv (November – December 1917) (C0071)

The first attempt by Soviet Russia (the Russian Soviet Republic) to liquidate Ukraine's independence by hijacking power at the All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets. The Bolshevik government (the Sovnarkom) planned to plant its delegates, artificially create a majority, and legally vote to transfer power to the Soviets under its control. The Ukrainian leadership recognized the threat and mobilized its supporters, leaving the aggressor's delegates in an absolute minority and thwarting the takeover[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Support for a Controlled Opposition (T0131)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/403):** Use by the Council of People's Commissars of local Bolshevik cells as a legal political force that was to speak on behalf of the Ukrainian proletariat against the Central Rada[2]. |
| **[Infiltration of Local Political Structures (T0132)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/404):** Deliberate transfer of loyal delegates and political agitators to the All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets in Kyiv in order to hijack the agenda from within[1]. |
| **[Seizure of Power Through Election Manipulation (T0133)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/405):** An attempt to convert an electoral minority into a procedural majority at the congress. Actual support was negligible: in the Constituent Assembly elections "across the country as a whole the Bolsheviks gathered less than 24% of the votes, and in the Ukrainian gubernias only 10%"[1]. Hence the wager on capturing representative bodies: the Central Committee of the RSDLP(b) declared outright that "the transfer of government from the hands of one soviet party into the hands of another party is secured without any revolution, by a simple decision of the Soviets, by a simple re-election of deputies to the Soviets," while the All-Russian Central Executive Committee's decree of 4 December 1917 "On the right of recall of delegates" provided the mechanism for such a replacement[1][3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Creation of a Puppet Government and Disguising the Intervention (December 1917 – Early 1918)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Creation of a Puppet Government and Disguising the Intervention (December 1917 – Early 1918) (C0072)

Having suffered defeat in Kyiv, the pro-Bolshevik delegates moved to Kharkiv, where they held an alternative congress and created a puppet government - the People's Secretariat, "the first Soviet government of Ukraine," created "as an alternative to the Ukrainian Central Rada and the General Secretariat of the Ukrainian Central Rada"[1]. This served as political cover for the start of the First Soviet-Ukrainian War (1917–1918) and allowed Soviet Russia to disguise the direct invasion by its troops as an internal civil war[2]. During the offensive, the aggressor provoked an uprising at the Arsenal plant in Kyiv, while the invasion itself was accompanied by heavy fighting for junction stations and the Battle of Kruty (January 1918), where the defense of the state was taken up by youth[3]. In February, the Red troops under the command of M. Muravyov - "the initiator of mass executions in the city"[1] - carried out a massacre in captured Kyiv. The campaign was halted by the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (February 1918), which brought the UNR international recognition and forced the RSFSR troops to retreat[2]. Hrushevsky - an eyewitness and head of the Central Rada - describes the preparation from within: "In Kyiv itself, from all sides, left and right alike, fierce agitation was waged against the Ukrainian government, the Central Rada, and Ukrainians as such. It brought the local Ukrainian regiments to near-total disintegration"[4].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (5)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Puppet Government (T0037)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/342):** The holding of an alternative congress in Kharkiv and the creation of a Moscow-controlled "People's Secretariat" to imitate an internal struggle: it was created "as an alternative to the Ukrainian Central Rada and the General Secretariat of the Ukrainian Central Rada" and "acted in close contact with and under the direct leadership of the highest state and party institutions of Soviet Russia"[1]. |
| **[Proxy War (T0018)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/326):** The use of the Kharkiv government as formal cover for external aggression, to present the military invasion as a civil war inside Ukraine: the People's Secretariat "announced the overthrow of the UCR and the recognition of only its own decrees as valid. It introduced the decrees of the Council of People's Commissars of Russia in Ukraine"[1][2]. |
| **[Staging a Coup (T0020)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/328):** The Bolsheviks' provocation of an uprising of the Arsenal plant workers in Kyiv itself at the very moment of the Red troops' offensive: it was "an armed action organized by the Kyiv committee of the Russian Social Democratic Workers' Party (Bolsheviks) against the Ukrainian Central Rada," and "it was planned for the moment of the approach of Soviet troops to Kyiv in the course of Soviet Russia's war against the UNR of 1917–18"[5]. |
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The direct deployment of Red troops, heavy fighting for the stations, and the storming of Kyiv. The Battle of Kruty took place "during the offensive on the city of Kyiv by the troops of Bolshevik Russia": advancing against the cadets and the student company was "a 6-thousand-strong Bolshevik detachment of Petrograd and Moscow Red Guards," and the defenders' losses amounted to "up to 300 killed, wounded, captured"[3]. The march on Kyiv was led by M. Muravyov: he "headed the march of Soviet troops on Kyiv in January 1918"[1]. Overall command was exercised by V. Antonov-Ovseenko: "in December 1917 - March 1918 - commissar for combating counter-revolution in the South, he led the Soviet troops in the struggle against otaman A. Kaledin and the Ukrainian Central Rada"[6]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** The Muravyov massacre of February 1918 after the capture of Kyiv by the Red troops: the EIU characterizes Muravyov as "the initiator of mass executions in the city," and later he was himself arrested on the charge of "'condoning mass executions and lootings that led to the fall of Soviet power in Ukraine'"[1]. Hrushevsky on the campaign's commander: "the chief commandant, the former gendarme Muravyov, who in February had boasted of executions of Ukrainians and the ruin of their property"[4]. |

</details>

posts.title: Second Armed Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Second Armed Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) (C0074)

After the withdrawal of the Austro-German troops, the Red Army of the RSFSR reoccupied most of Ukraine. The aggressor launched a large-scale extraction of resources: special food-requisition detachments forcibly confiscated grain and raw materials from villagers for export to the RSFSR. The resistance of the local population, which erupted into powerful revolts of the insurgent front (including the uprising of Otaman Hryhoriv), was brutally suppressed by punitive expeditions and mass terror by the Cheka and the army. The campaign was aggravated by the intervention of the White Guard troops of General Denikin, which led to the "Kyiv Catastrophe" (August 1919), when the Ukrainian troops were forced to surrender the liberated capital[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (10)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** A full-scale offensive by the Ukrainian Front of the Red Army in early 1919 to recapture Ukrainian cities after the withdrawal of Austro-German troops[1]. The Red Army's counteroffensive in the fall and winter of 1919 against Denikin's forces, as a result of which the Bolsheviks recaptured Kyiv on December 16 and occupied most of Ukraine[1]. The invasion of General Denikin's troops under the slogan of restoring a "united and indivisible Russia" and the armed ousting of Ukrainian units from Kyiv, which they had liberated, on August 31, 1919 (the "Kyiv catastrophe"), leading to the collapse of the front[1]. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** Forcible requisitioning ("prodrazverstka") and the non-stop export of grain, coal, and raw materials to the RSFSR without economic compensation, which provoked uprisings, among them Hryhoriv's[1]. |
| **[Economic Control (T0038)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/343):** Introduction of a state monopoly on the grain trade and centralized control over the distribution of goods[1]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Systematic, demonstrative violence and intimidation by the forces of the Cheka (the All-Ukrainian Cheka, VUChK) to create an atmosphere of total fear and to coerce the peasantry into surrendering food[2]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** Mass executions by shooting of unarmed civilians and participants in suppressed peasant uprisings, carried out by punitive detachments to physically eliminate pockets of resistance[1]. |
| **[Punitive Expeditions (T0077)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** Use of military units and food requisition detachments for forcible raids on Ukrainian villages to confiscate grain[2]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The White Guard command's refusal to recognize Ukrainian statehood. Denikin's programmatic appeal "To the Population of Little Russia" declared the struggle for a Ukrainian state to be treason: Petliura and his associates, "who initiated the dismemberment of Russia, continue even now to carry out their evil work of creating an independent 'Ukrainian State' and of fighting against the rebirth of a United Russia"[3]. The Ukrainian language was demoted to a "Little Russian popular language," while Russian was declared the state language: "declaring the Russian language the state language throughout the whole expanse of Russia, I consider entirely inadmissible and forbid the persecution of the Little Russian popular language"[3]. After the "Kyiv catastrophe" of 31 August 1919, Ukrainian troops were forced to withdraw to the line of Vasylkiv[2]. The executor was General Bredov: "White Guard units of General M. Bredov entered Kyiv from the left bank across the unguarded Dnipro bridges. An armed clash took place on Duma Square"[2]. |
| **[Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language (T0114.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/379):** General Denikin's occupation policy aimed at destroying Ukrainian culture by abolishing the right to education in one's native language and by the outright closure of Ukrainian schools[1]. |
| **[Legislative Ban on the Native Language (T0113.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/374):** The White Guard command's ban on the printing and distribution of Ukrainian books in the captured territories[2]. |
| **[Liquidation of National Civic Organizations (T0128)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** Forced closure of Ukrainian cultural and educational institutions by the White Guard administration[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) (C0075)

The final destruction of Ukrainian sovereignty through the imposition of treaties on a so-called military-political union. While formally preserving the status of an independent republic, the leadership of the RSFSR de facto brought the key Ukrainian agencies — military, financial, economic, and transport — under its direct control. The final chord in the suppression of organized armed resistance, and a symbol of its tragic end, was the execution by the Bolsheviks of 359 captured soldiers of the UNR Army near Bazar in November 1921[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Sham Treaties (T0088)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/360):** Use of the "union treaty" format of June 1, 1919, and December 28, 1920, not to create an equal federation but as an instrument for legalizing direct, rigid rule from Moscow[1]. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Transfer of control over the military affairs, finances, communications, and transport routes of the Ukrainian republic into the hands of the central bodies of the RSFSR[1]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** De facto liquidation of the Ukrainian army (the disbandment of the Ukrainian Front) and the transformation of the government of the Ukrainian SSR into a nominal appendage of the Russian administrative machine[1]. |
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The signing of the Treaty of Riga in March 1921: a backroom division of spheres of influence and Ukrainian territories with Poland behind the back of the Ukrainian people, legalized through the formal participation of the puppet Ukrainian SSR[2]. |
| **[Installation of a New System of Governance (T0036)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/341):** Moscow's seizure of direct control over the punitive apparatus through the decision to liquidate the independent All-Ukrainian Cheka (VUChK) in August 1919 and the appointment of its own special commissar, Ya. Peters[1]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Coercion of legal Ukrainian parties into self-dissolution (in particular, the Borotbists in the spring of 1920) and their absorption by the CP(b)U through political blackmail and the bribery of their leaders with official posts[1]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** The tragedy near Bazar in November 1921: the execution by the Bolsheviks of 359 captured UNR soldiers who refused to defect to the Reds, as a symbol of the end of organized resistance[2]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

posts.title: Legal Absorption through the Creation of the USSR (1922–1924)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Legal Absorption through the Creation of the USSR (1922–1924) (C0076)

Formal consolidation of the seizure of Ukraine by dragging it into the so-called Union of SSRs. The unification of equal republics with the right of free secession was declared, but in practice the union treaty (December 1922) and the Constitution of the USSR (1924) became instruments of rigid centralization. The Ukrainian SSR was definitively stripped of control over foreign policy, the army, foreign trade, transport, and communications — all these spheres passed to the jurisdiction of union-level people's commissariats in Moscow[1][2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Sham Treaties (T0088)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/360):** Use of the Treaty on the Creation of the USSR to formally declare a union of equal republics, masking the final centralization of power in Moscow[2]. |
| **[Restriction of Sovereignty (T0031)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/338):** Stripping the Ukrainian SSR of control over foreign policy, the army, foreign trade, transport, and communications through the 1924 Constitution of the USSR, transferring them to the jurisdiction of the all-union people's commissariats[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) (C0077)

An assault on the traditional way of life of the Ukrainian village, which remained the principal bearer of national identity and economic independence. Under the slogans of socialist modernization, Moscow proclaimed the course of "the liquidation of the kulaks as a class": the secret Politburo resolution of January 30, 1930 ordered "to confiscate from the kulaks of these districts the means of production, livestock, farm and residential buildings, processing enterprises, fodder and seed stocks" and to send "60,000 to concentration camps and subject 150,000 kulaks to deportation to remote districts," of which for Ukraine - 15 thousand to concentration camps and 30–35 thousand to deportation[1]. Peasants who put up resistance were dispossessed en masse and deported to Siberia and the North[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (5)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Economic Control (T0038)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/343):** Forcible seizure of land, livestock, and agricultural implements from peasants as part of forced collectivization under slogans of socialist modernization[2]. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** Mass dispossession and forced deportation of hundreds of thousands of resisting peasants (the so-called "kurkuls") to remote special settlements in Siberia and the North[2]. |
| **[Deportation (T0127)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/399):** Mass deportation of hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian peasants ("kulaks") and their family members to Siberia and remote northern regions of the USSR[2]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Mass arrests of peasants during the dekulakization campaign: according to the 1930 directives, in addition to deportations, tens of thousands of people were sent directly to concentration camps for isolation[2]. |
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** Use of dekulakized peasants, sent into the emerging GULAG system, as forced unpaid labor for heavy state projects[2]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

1. Политбюро ЦК ВКП(б), 30 января 1930. (1930). О мероприятиях по ликвидации кулацких хозяйств в районах сплошной коллективизации.
2. Лариса Якубова. (2013). Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.).

posts.title: Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) (C0078)

The use of artificial famine as a weapon of mass destruction for the physical and psychological suppression of national resistance. The launch of a merciless grain-procurement machine, the confiscation of absolutely all food, the introduction of the "blackboard" regime (a total blockade of settlements)[1], and a ban prohibiting peasants from leaving the starving districts: the directive of Stalin and Molotov of January 22, 1933 ordered "not to allow the mass departure of peasants from Ukraine to other regions," declaring the flight of the starving "for bread" a plot "organized by enemies of Soviet power, SRs and agents of Poland"[2]. Physical extermination was accompanied by total psychological terror and show trials[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (6)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Artificial Famine (T0121)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/393):** Confiscation of absolutely all food, including the extraction of seed stocks, through the mechanism of crushing grain procurement quotas, which led to mass deadly famine[3]. |
| **[Economic Blockade (T0108)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/368):** The introduction of the "blackboard" regime - a total economic blockade of settlements. The resolution of the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR and the CC of the CP(b)U of December 6, 1932, signed by Chubar and Kosior, prescribed "the immediate cessation of the delivery of goods, the complete cessation of cooperative and state trade on site, and the removal of all available goods from the respective cooperative and state shops," as well as "a complete ban on kolkhoz trade both for kolkhozes and kolkhoz members and for individual farmers"[1]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** Deliberately starving millions of Ukrainian peasants to death as a direct result of Moscow's state policy[3]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Systematic psychological suppression through public show trials of "saboteurs" and the introduction of the punitive law on the protection of socialist property (the "law of five ears of grain")[3]. |
| **[Transport Blockade (T0107)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/367):** Sealing off the starving region: peasants who tried to escape from the blockaded villages were intercepted on roads and at railway junctions. The directive sealed off precisely Ukraine and the Kuban: "all peasants who had managed to leave Ukraine and the North Caucasus were subject to return to their places of residence," while permits to leave were denied even "to the national districts of the krai, where there was no famine at all"[3]. Within 50 days "219.5 thousand peasants were detained, including 38 thousand in the Ukrainian SSR, 47 thousand in the North Caucasus, 44 thousand in the Central Black Earth region, 5 thousand in the Western oblast, 65 thousand on the railways"; of these, "186.5 thousand were sent home under convoy, almost 3 thousand were convicted, and all the rest awaited trial or were under investigation in filtration camps"[3]. The point of the operation lay not in sentences but in marching people back into the starving villages: the coded telegram "documentarily attests to his intention to organize absolute famine in the rural areas of Ukraine"[3]. |
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** Lethally dangerous exploitation of the labor of Ukrainian peasants, convicted en masse under the "law of five ears of grain" and exiled to corrective labor camps during the Holodomor[3]. |

</details>

posts.title: Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) (C0079)

The abrupt rollback of the policy of "Ukrainization." The start of the physical extermination and political defamation of the intellectual elite - writers, scholars, film directors, as well as the old national communists (M. Skrypnyk was driven to suicide)[1]. In parallel with the physical terror came the destruction of the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church, large-scale censorship, the rewriting of history, and the artificial convergence of the Ukrainian language with Russian; works published in the Ukrainian SSR before 1933, in the words of the compiler of the anthology "Executed Renaissance," were "destroyed as a result of Moscow's new course toward the rout and colonial provincialization of Ukraine"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Creation of an atmosphere of total paralyzing fear in society through the fabrication of cases (for example, the "Union for the Liberation of Ukraine") and the staging of public show trials[1]. |
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** Mass confiscation and destruction of literature declared "nationalist," and rigid control over the printed word and the arts[1]. |
| **[Linguistic Assimilation (T0113)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/373):** The forced orthography reform of 1933, aimed at artificially bringing Ukrainian grammar and terminology closer to the Russian language[1]. |
| **[Seizure of Religious Institutions (T0100)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/362):** Mass closure and destruction of churches, as well as repressions against clergy, aimed at the complete destruction of the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church (UAOC)[1]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Physical annihilation and isolation of the Ukrainian intelligentsia, writers, and scholars, as well as of the party opposition (national communists), in the course of targeted repressions. Fabrication of cases (including the "UNC" case) and driving representatives of the national elite to death, including the historian Mykhailo Hrushevsky, the writer Mykola Khvylovy, and People's Commissar Mykola Skrypnyk[1]. |
| **[Destruction of Historical Memory (T0045)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/349):** Institutional destruction of national historical scholarship, closure of research schools, and removal of the works of Ukrainian historians from scholarly circulation[1]. |
| **[Rewriting of History (T0004)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** The construction of a new Soviet-imperial historical canon to supplant the Ukrainian past: "from the late 1930s a thesis took hold in the historical scholarship of the USSR," proclaimed in the works of B. Grekov, K. Huslystyi, and F. Yastrebov, "of Kyivan Rus as the 'common cradle' of the history of the Ukrainian, Russian, and Belarusian peoples," and "in 1939 B. Grekov advanced the proposition of the ethnic unity of the 'Rus people' in the era of Kyivan Rus"[3]. This scheme displaced M. Hrushevsky's conception and denied the independence of Ukraine's history. |

</details>
