posts.title: NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: NKVD National Operations and Institutional Russification (1937–1939) (C0080)

The total purge of ethnic minorities (Poles, Germans, Greeks, Bulgarians) during the Great Terror through targeted national orders of the NKVD. In parallel, in 1938, Moscow officially liquidated every single national district and minority school - by resolutions of the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 24 January 1938[1][2] - and by the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the USSR Council of People's Commissars of 13 March 1938 No. 324 made the study of the Russian language compulsory[3]; Kyiv executed the decision by the resolution of the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U of 10 April 1938[4], returning to overtly imperial practices of assimilation[5][6].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Extermination Based on Identity (T0120)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/392):** The conduct of secret mass "national operations" of the NKVD for the physical annihilation of members of ethnic minorities[6]. The mechanism was set by the operational orders of people's commissar Yezhov: No. 00485 of 11 August 1937 opened the Polish operation - "to begin, from 20 August 1937, a broad operation aimed at the complete liquidation of the local organizations of the 'POW'" with completion "within a three-month term"[7], - and No. 00439 of 25 July 1937 the German one[8]; the Greek, Bulgarian and other operations followed their template[6]. The scale is recorded in the perpetrator's own accounting: according to the summary figures of the 1st Special Department of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR dated 30 August 1938, 94,659 people were arrested in the republic under orders Nos. 00485, 00593 and others (54,011 on the Polish line, 23,036 on the German, 5,642 on the Greek), of whom 61,683 had been convicted by 1 July 1938; in all, of the 197,945 people convicted by the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR over the reporting period, 122,274 were sentenced to be shot - nearly two out of every three[9]. Across all the "national lines" of the USSR, 335,513 people were convicted, and 73.66% of them were shot[10]. |
| **[Liquidation of National Civic Organizations (T0128)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/400):** The forcible closure of all national councils, pedagogical institutes, theaters and cultural institutions of ethnic minorities in the Ukrainian SSR[5]: the national districts and village soviets were liquidated by the resolution of the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of 24 January 1938[2], and the resolution of the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U of 10 April 1938 reorganized the national schools and colleges and turned the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute into an institute of foreign languages[4]. |
| **[Conversion of Schools to the Metropole's Language (T0114.003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/379):** On 24 January 1938 the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b), by its resolution "On the Liquidation of National Schools and National Sections in Schools," closed non-Russian schools throughout the Union, liquidating the national districts and village soviets on the same day[1][2]; on 13 March the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the USSR Council of People's Commissars No. 324 "On the Compulsory Study of the Russian Language in the Schools of the National Republics and Regions" made the metropole's language a compulsory subject in all schools of the republics[3]. Kyiv executed the decision on 10 April 1938: the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U, "proceeding from the decision of the Central Committee of the VKP(b)," declared "the further existence of special national schools inexpedient and harmful" and resolved to reorganize the German, Polish, Czech, Swedish and other schools and technical colleges "into Soviet schools of the ordinary type," to liquidate national sections and classes at ordinary schools, colleges and universities, and, where there was nowhere to transfer the pupils, to transfer the institutions themselves to ordinary school curricula - "with instruction in Ukrainian or Russian"; the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute was turned into an institute of foreign languages, and all the work was ordered finished by 1 August 1938[4]. The Politburo wrote its justification into the resolution itself: "enemies of the people - Trotskyites, Bukharinites and bourgeois nationalists operating in the People's Commissariat of Education of the Ukrainian SSR - implanted special national German, Polish, Czech, Swedish, Greek and other schools, turning them into hotbeds of bourgeois-nationalist, anti-Soviet influence on children"[4]. The decision was given the form of a state act by the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR in its resolution of 29 June 1938 on the reorganization of special national schools, colleges and the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute: by 1 August 1938, 766 national primary, incomplete secondary and secondary schools were subject to reorganization into ordinary schools with (predominantly) Russian and Ukrainian as the language of instruction, and another 122 were merged with Russian and Ukrainian ones on the territorial principle - the count of the historian Liudmyla Yakubova[11]. |

</details>

posts.title: Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) (C0081)

The collusion of two totalitarian regimes (the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact), which led to the USSR's invasion of Poland and the seizure of Western Ukraine. To legitimize the occupation, the "People's Assembly of Western Ukraine 1939" was staged, which "on October 27 in Lviv… adopted the Declaration on the reunification of Western Ukraine with the Ukrainian SSR"[1]. Then came the mass deportations: "Between September 1939 and June 1941, up to 1,250,000 people (about 10% of the population) were removed from these lands and Western Belarus… to remote regions of the USSR"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (8)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The partition of Eastern Europe behind the backs of its peoples: the secret protocol established that "in the event of a territorial-political rearrangement of the areas belonging to the Polish state, the boundary of the spheres of interest of Germany and the USSR shall run approximately along the line of the rivers Narew, Vistula, and San"[3]. Half a century later the Congress of People's Deputies of the USSR "recognizes the secret protocols as legally untenable and invalid from the moment of their signing"[4]. The invasion was covered by Molotov's note to the Polish ambassador Grzybowski (17 September 1939): "the Polish state and its government have in fact ceased to exist"[5]. |
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The direct armed invasion of Polish territory by the Red Army on September 17, 1939 for the military occupation of the western Ukrainian lands; the seizure was consolidated by "the treaty of the USSR with Germany (September 28, 1939)," which "confirmed the incorporation of the western Ukrainian lands into the USSR"[6]. |
| **[Sham Expression of Popular Will (T0109)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** The staging of a no-alternative "People's Assembly" under the control of occupation troops to give the seizure legal form: "On October 27 in Lviv, the People's Assembly of Western Ukraine of 1939 adopted the Declaration on the reunification of Western Ukraine with the Ukrainian SSR, and on November 1 the Supreme Soviet of the USSR passed the law admitting Western Ukraine, as part of the Ukrainian SSR, into the USSR"[1]. |
| **[Annexation of Territories (T0017)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/325):** The official annexation of the occupied lands: the western Ukrainian lands were incorporated into the USSR under the treaty with Germany of September 28, 1939[6], and "after the Red Army occupied Bessarabia and Northern Bukovyna at the end of June 1940, on August 2, 1940 the Supreme Soviet of the USSR annexed Northern Bukovyna and the Khotyn, Akkerman, and Izmail districts of Bessarabia to the Ukrainian SSR"[1]. |
| **[Deportation (T0127)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/399):** Mass forced resettlement by quota: "under the resolutions of the Council of People's Commissars of December 5, 1939 and March 2, 1940, subject to administrative resettlement were the employees of the former state institutions, courts, police, army, merchants, Polish settlers, landowners, owners of plants and factories, and their families"; in total "up to 1,250,000 people were removed to remote regions of the USSR"[2]. The waves were separate: the osadniks were deported under the USSR Sovnarkom resolution of December 5, 1939, no. 2010-558ss - its text remains in the closed Archive of the President of the Russian Federation (fond 93), while the mechanics of the operation are known from the NKVD Instruction approved on December 29, 1939[7]; the families of officers, policemen and prison guards were deported under the resolution of March 2, 1940, no. 289-127ss[8]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The neutralization of the politically active stratum through mass arrests: immediately after the "People's Assembly" came "the arrests of leading figures of the Ukrainian intelligentsia, by lists prepared in advance, drawn up in the Soviet consulate"[9]; "in all, in 1939—1941 the NKVD organs arrested 21,982 Poles, 23,163 Ukrainians and 13,160 Jews"[9], and those arrested faced execution, prison or the GULAG camps: "in total, during 1939—1941, between 16 and 35 thousand OUN members were shot or imprisoned"[9]. |
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The transfer of hundreds of thousands of people into special settlements and camps as a system of forced labor: in under two years "up to 1,250,000 people were removed to remote regions of the USSR"[2] – the deportees were assigned to labor in remote regions with no right to leave. |
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** The sign of the new order goes up within the very first weeks: Soviet troops took Lviv on 22 September 1939[10], and already in October, in the city center, on the islet in the middle of today's Svobody Avenue, rose the monument to the Stalin Constitution - a huge vertical composition of columns entwined with red banners, on a wooden frame, with five sculptural groups (a Red Army soldier, a worker, a mother with a child, a female student, and an old Hutsul with a boy) and inscriptions in Ukrainian, Polish and Yiddish symbolizing the "friendship of peoples" according to the articles of the Stalin constitution[11][12]. The sign has named authors: the sculptor Serhii Lytvynenko and the Kyiv artist Mykhailo Dmytrenko, who arrived in Lviv in 1939 in the "landing party" of Soviet artists whose task was the implantation of socialist realism; possibly the authors merely adapted to the site a design produced in Moscow, and it was executed by the sculptors Yevhen Dzyndra and Andrii Koverko[11]. The monument stood until 30 June 1941 and vanished with the arrival of the Germans[11]. |

</details>

posts.title: Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) (C0082)

The Soviet authorities' treatment of Ukraine as a colonial resource during the war. During the 1941 retreat the directive of the USSR Sovnarkom and the Central Committee of 29 June 1941 was in force: "In the forced withdrawal of Red Army units… leave the enemy not a kilogram of grain, not a liter of fuel… All valuable property… that cannot be evacuated must without fail be destroyed"[1]. In 1943–1944, on the liberated territory, the mobilization of the "chornosvytnyky" was carried out: they were "thrown into combat often at once, without undergoing military training… sometimes unarmed, not even changed into military uniform"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Total Destruction of Infrastructure (T0105)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/366):** The 1941 scorched-earth tactic under the directive of the USSR Sovnarkom and the Central Committee of 29 June 1941: "In the forced withdrawal of Red Army units, drive off the rolling railway stock, leave the enemy not a single locomotive, not a single railcar"[1]; the Dnipro hydroelectric station was "destroyed at the beginning of the Great Patriotic War… (see the Directive of the USSR Council of People's Commissars and the Central Committee of the VKP(b) of June 29, 1941)"[3]. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** The total removal of industrial equipment and food supplies into the interior of the USSR: "550 industrial facilities were moved into the interior of the USSR (190 of all-Union and 360 of republican subordination)"; "From the Right Bank to the left bank of the Dnipro were ferried 4,498 tractors, 680 combines, 690 motor vehicles"[4]. |
| **[Forced Mobilization (T0049)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/351):** The mass conscription by field draft offices of the population of just-liberated territories: "'Chornosvytnyky' or 'black infantry' – such was the unofficial name given to men and youths mobilized by field military commissariats, and in fact by the commanders of formations, units, and detachments in 1943–1944 after the Red Army's liberation of enemy-occupied territories"[2]. |
| **[Use as Cannon Fodder (T0134)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/406):** The use of untrained conscripts as expendable material: they were "thrown into combat often at once, without undergoing military training in reserve units, sometimes unarmed, not even changed into military uniform (hence the name)"[2]. The scale is visible from a single episode: "after the Red Army first took Kharkiv in the spring of 1943, about 15 thousand people aged 15 to 45 were mobilized into it and sent to the front without training," with "1 rifle per 5-10 men"[2]. |

</details>

## List of Materials

2. Р. І. Пилявець (Воєнно-історичний вісник, 2019, № 1). (2019). «Чорна піхота» як історичне явище.

posts.title: Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) (C0084)

A war waged by NKVD/MGB troops against the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) in western Ukraine: chekist-military operations, mass repressive actions, and the forced removal of insurgents' families to Siberia - in 1944–52 "203,662 people were deported from the territory of Western Ukraine to special settlements in remote regions of the USSR"[1]. Its finale was the use of collusion with a third party - Operation "Vistula" (1947), coordinated with the pro-Soviet government of Poland, "the concluding stage of the forced deportation of Ukrainians" "from the ancestral lands of Lemkivshchyna, Nadsiannia, Kholmshchyna, and Pidliashshia," carried out to deprive the UPA of its social base[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (7)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Punitive Expeditions (T0077)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** Regular chekist-military operations by the NKVD and MGB to sweep western Ukrainian villages: the People's Commissar of Internal Affairs of the Ukrainian SSR T. Strokach personally "directed and coordinated operational-chekist operations to liquidate the underground of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and units of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, and mass deportations of the population in Western Ukraine"[3]. Already "on April 5, 1944, on the basis of a directive of the People's Commissariat of Internal Affairs of the USSR, a scheme of arrests and deportation of OUN–UPA members was worked out"[1]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** Extrajudicial killings of civilians in the course of suppressing the insurgency: the Presidium of the CPSU Central Committee itself admitted, in its resolution "On the Political and Economic Situation of the Western Oblasts of the Ukrainian SSR" of May 26, 1953: "From 1944 through 1952, up to 500 thousand people in the western oblasts of Ukraine were subjected to various kinds of repression, including over 134 thousand arrested, over 153 thousand killed, and over 203 thousand deported forever from the Ukrainian SSR"[4][5] – the authorities did not divide the killed into insurgents and civilians, and already on July 2, 1953, after Beria's arrest, the resolution itself was revoked as conducive to "the activization of bourgeois-nationalist elements"[4]. Terror was also waged by disguised MGB "special groups" acting under the guise of the UPA: the military prosecutor of the MVD troops of the Ukrainian district, Kosharsky, in his report to Khrushchev (February 15, 1949), cited "examples of beatings, rapes and robberies of the population" by agent-fighters and stated: "the actions of the so-called MGB special groups are of a pronounced bandit, anti-Soviet character and, of course, cannot be justified by any operational considerations"[6]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** The creation of an atmosphere of total fear through the bloody provocations of NKVD special groups operating in the guise of the UPA: People's Commissar Strokach "initiated the formation of special groups of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR from former partisans for the struggle against the UPA" and "personally interrogated the captured leaders of the OUN networks of Western Ukraine"[3]. The terror was also demonstrative: "one of the forms of struggle was the policy of intimidating OUN and UPA members and the local population: open trials and executions, putting the bodies of the dead on public display, and destroying insurgent graves"[7]. |
| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** The coordination of actions with the pro-Soviet government of Poland to destroy the Ukrainian underground: Operation "Vistula," "as a deportation action, was elaborated in detail and carried out by the Polish authorities," but its execution "was coordinated with the party-Soviet organs of power of the USSR" - the Soviet command transferred "from Lviv oblast one tank division and special NKVD units, and blocked the Ukrainian-Polish border with border troops"[2]. |
| **[Deportation (T0127)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/399):** The forcible removal of insurgents' families to Siberia and the deportation of the Ukrainians of Zakerzonnia: the removal of "bandit accomplices" with their entire families began at once - already in the summer of 1944 "more than 17,000 people were carried off to Krasnoyarsk Krai"[1]; in all, in 1944–52, 203,662 people were removed to special settlements, among them "representatives of the families of members of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and soldiers of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and their sympathizers — 182,543 people"[1]. Operation "Vistula" was carried out in order to "deprive it of socio-economic and moral-psychological support from the local Ukrainian population," and ended in the scattering of the community: the authorities rid themselves of the Ukrainian population, "dispersing about 150 thousand people"[2]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Mass arrests of UPA fighters, OUN members, and those suspected of aiding them, followed by dispatch to the GULAG camps, upon which the regime placed "the isolation of 'unreliable elements'" as one of its key tasks[5]. During Operation "Vistula," for civilians suspected of assisting the underground there was provision for "the introduction of courts-martial and concentration camps, in particular at Jaworzno"[2]. By 1951 Ukrainians had become the second-largest nation of the GULAG: according to the agency's own statistics, the "National composition of GULAG prisoners (as of January 1, 1951)" counted 506,221 Ukrainians out of some 2.5 million prisoners - about 20%[8]. |
| **[Labor Exploitation (T0057)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/356):** The use of captured resistance members and deportees as free labor: the tasks of the GULAG included "using them as cheap labor and transferring them, as needed, from place to place"[5]; deportees from Western Ukraine were sent to special settlements and hard labor - in the summer of 1944 alone "more than 17,000 people were carried off to Krasnoyarsk Krai"[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Postwar Ideological Terror ("Zhdanovshchina") (1946–1953) (C0085)

A return to total control over culture after the relative relaxations of the war years: the rout of the Ukrainian creative intelligentsia, accusations of "bourgeois nationalism" (attacks on Rylsky, Yanovsky, the persecution of Sosiura for the poem "Love Ukraine"). In parallel ran a state antisemitic campaign: "On July 18, 1952 the Military Collegium of the USSR Supreme Court passed death sentences on 13 people, including 5 natives of Ukraine… on August 12, 1952 they were all executed"[1], and in January 1953 the "Doctors' Plot" began.

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (3)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Censorship (T0101)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/363):** Total ideological control over art and the press, the banning of works and the vilification of writers for alleged "bourgeois nationalism." The campaign culminated in the verdict in the case of the Jewish Anti-Fascist Committee: "on July 18, 1952 the Military Collegium of the USSR Supreme Court passed death sentences on 13 people, including 5 natives of Ukraine, well-known Jewish writers and poets"[1]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** The staging of public political persecution (attacks on Rylsky, Sosiura, Yanovsky, the campaign against "cosmopolitans"), instilling an atmosphere of fear. Its outcome was the execution of the defendants in the JAC case: "on August 12, 1952 they were all executed"[1]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** Fabricated repressions against figures of the Ukrainian and Jewish intelligentsia: in the case of the Jewish Anti-Fascist Committee, "on July 18, 1952 the Military Collegium of the USSR Supreme Court passed death sentences on 13 people, including 5 natives of Ukraine, the well-known Jewish writers and poets D. Bergelson, D. Hofshtein, L. Kvitko, P. Markish, I. Fefer. On August 12, 1952 they were all executed"[1]. |

</details>

posts.title: Suppression of the GULAG Uprisings (1953–1954)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Suppression of the GULAG Uprisings (1953–1954) (C0086)

After Stalin's death, the amnesty did not extend to political prisoners, among whom Ukrainians made up an enormous share. This provoked large-scale uprisings within the concentration camp system (Vorkuta, Norilsk, Kengir). In Kengir, the insurgents created a system of self-government, a radio station, and workshops for making weapons, demanding the arrival of a commission of the CPSU Central Committee. During the suppression of the Norilsk uprising, "about 100 people were killed and more than 200 wounded"[1]. In Kengir, the authorities sent in the army: "1,600 soldiers, 3 fire engines, and 5 tanks moved into the zone. It was the only suppression of camp uprisings with tanks in Soviet history"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (2)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Punitive Expeditions (T0077)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/359):** Use of regular troops and tanks to suppress revolts of Ukrainian political prisoners in the concentration camp system. In Kengir, tanks crushed the unarmed: "About 200 Ukrainian women joined hands and marched against the tanks. But the tanks did not stop and one by one overcame the living phalanx. And the MVD men rushed to the barracks, shooting everyone they encountered"[2]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** Mass killings of prisoners during the forcible suppression of the uprisings. In Norilsk, "about 100 people were killed and more than 200 wounded"[1]; in Kengir, "during the suppression of the uprising, about 700 prisoners were killed or wounded"[2]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Ideological Campaign of the "300th Anniversary of Reunification" and the Transfer of Crimea (1954)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Ideological Campaign of the "300th Anniversary of Reunification" and the Transfer of Crimea (1954) (C0087)

A state propaganda operation: to mask Ukraine's colonial status, the empire celebrated with pomp the anniversary of the Pereiaslav Council, constructing the myth of a "single people." As part of the same campaign, Crimea was transferred to the Ukrainian SSR – the decree of the USSR Supreme Soviet Presidium of 19 February 1954 motivated it thus: "Taking into account the commonality of the economy, territorial proximity, and close economic and cultural ties between the Crimean oblast and the Ukrainian SSR"[1]. The real context of the decision: "After the Second World War, the deportation of the Crimean Tatar people and mass resettlements from other regions of the USSR, the peninsula is in a deep socio-economic crisis," and "Moscow admits ever more openly: the Crimean region is a problem territory that the union center does not know how to sustain"[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Rewriting of History (T0004)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** A state campaign to construct a historical myth: the "Theses on the 300th Anniversary of the Reunification of Ukraine with Russia," approved by the CPSU Central Committee, declared that "by this historic act was completed the long struggle of the freedom-loving Ukrainian people against foreign enslavers for reunification with the Russian people in a single Russian state"[3] – the annexation of 1654 was retroactively rewritten as the goal and outcome of a national struggle. |
| **[Denial of a Distinct Identity (T0010)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/319):** The imposition of a concept of unbreakable unity instead of recognizing a distinct nation: per the Theses, "by the act of reunification the Ukrainian people consolidated its close and unbreakable historical bond with the Russian people, in whom it found a great ally, a faithful friend and defender"[3]. The celebrations and the transfer of Crimea "taking into account the commonality of the economy, territorial proximity, and close economic and cultural ties"[1] served the same frame. |
| **[Administrative-Territorial Division (T0030)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/337):** The redrawing of internal borders by the USSR Supreme Soviet Presidium's resolution of 19 February 1954: "To approve the joint submission of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the RSFSR and the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR on the transfer of the Crimean oblast from the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic to the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic"[1] – the decision was taken in Moscow, without any expression of will by the peninsula's inhabitants. Behind the "commonality of the economy" stood the desire to shift the peninsula, ruined by deportation and war, onto the books of the Ukrainian SSR: "Moscow admits ever more openly: the Crimean region is a problem territory that the union center does not know how to sustain"[2]. |
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** The jubilee was fixed with a material sign in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, on the very square where the rada had taken place in 1654. The sign went up in the course of the jubilee reconstruction of the town ordered by the republic's authorities: "in connection with the preparation for the celebration of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia," the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR allocated 20 million rubles for the reconstruction of Pereiaslav-Khmelnytskyi, the reconstruction plan was developed under the direction of the architect Volodymyr Zabolotnyi, and in May 1954, "on the square where the historic Pereiaslav Rada took place (now Reunification Square), an obelisk with a memorial plaque was erected"[4]. On the plaque, beneath a relief of Bohdan Khmelnytsky, a text is cast: "On this square, on 8 (18) January 1654, the Pereiaslav Rada took place, which, expressing the will of the Ukrainian people, unanimously adopted the historic decision on the reunification of Ukraine with Russia"[5]. The sign did not merely mark the spot: it declared the decision unanimous and expressive of the people's will, fixing this version in bronze on the very square where it all happened. |

</details>

# Campaign: Information Blockade Around the Chornobyl Disaster (1986) (C0090)

After the explosion at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant, the union center concealed the scale of the radiation threat: "the concealment of information about the catastrophe from the public was initiated by the country's leadership," and "the maps of radioactive contamination of lands remained classified until 1990"[1]. People were deprived of the right to protection - "the population was not warned of the danger and was given no recommendations," and, "despite the fact that in Kyiv the radiation dose rate increased more than a hundredfold, neither the May Day demonstration nor the Peace Cycling Race was cancelled"[1][2].

# Campaign: Stalling Democratic Reforms and Countering the People's Movement (Rukh) (1989–1990) (C0091)

The conservative party apparatus under the leadership of V. Shcherbytsky attempted to contain the growth of the national liberation movement. Because of KGB pressure and the threat of an immediate ban, the founders of the Ukrainian independence movement were initially forced to disguise their goals, naming the organization the "People's Movement of Ukraine for Perestroika": "at first it supported the official course of perestroika, without formally raising the demand of Ukraine's independence," and its program "lacked the demand for a new union treaty and contained a formal provision recognizing the 'guiding role' of the communist party"[1]. Only in 1990, having proclaimed that "what is needed is not perestroika but the complete dismantling of the totalitarian system," did Rukh remove the words "for perestroika" from its name[1].

---

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Creation of Agents of Influence (T0013)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/322):** The use of brute force by party activists against Rukh activists: when Rukh members attempted to install a cross on the grave of those executed near Bazar, "the activists were not allowed into the village" "with the help of KGB men and provocations about the Rukh members' 'Banderite' intentions"; some participants "were dragged out of the car, beaten, and the flags were torn to shreds," while the role of "protesting peasants" was played by men in disguise: "in reality these were communist party activists from nearby districts"[2]. The political prisoner Vasyl Ovsienko ended up in the hospital: "the communists thrashed me near Bazar on November 17"[3]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The forcible neutralization of movement activists at the hands of the security structures and party apparatus: the dispersal of commemorative actions with beatings ("dragged out of the car, beaten") with the participation of the KGB and the militia[2], the hospitalization of the beaten political prisoner Vasyl Ovsienko[3], and the death of Rukh member Yevhen Melenivsky - after a "conversation" at the regional MVD directorate he "died on his way home"[4], and later - the law enforcement bodies' demonstrative disinterest in solving crimes against Rukh functionaries: they "demonstratively displayed disinterest in solving the crime"[5]. |
| **[Abduction of People (T0053)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/354):** The forced disappearance of a key functionary of the movement: "on the night of January 15–16, 1994, two armed unknown men burst into the NRU secretariat in Kyiv, took some documents, and searched for Boichyshyn" - Mykhailo Boichyshyn, head of the Rukh secretariat, was never seen again. The investigation was sabotaged: law enforcement "at first was in no hurry to accept the report of the politician's disappearance, and then demonstratively displayed disinterest in solving the crime," and "the investigators were interested not so much in the circumstances of the attack on the Secretariat and Boichyshyn's disappearance as in the party's financing"[5]. |

# Campaign: Manipulative Referendum on the Preservation of the USSR (March 1991) (C0093)

Moscow's attempt to legitimize the preservation of a disintegrating empire. The all-Union ballot contained the question: "Do you consider necessary the preservation of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics as a renewed federation of equal sovereign republics in which the rights and freedoms of a person of any nationality will be fully guaranteed"[1]. The Verkhovna Rada of the Ukrainian SSR added its own question – on Ukraine's membership in the Union "on the basis of the Declaration of State Sovereignty of Ukraine"[2], which is what made the outcome ambiguous. The ambiguous wording was approved by the USSR Supreme Soviet in a resolution signed by its chairman Lukyanov[1].

# Campaign: Attempted Coup d'État by the GKChP (August 1991) (C0095)

An armed mutiny by the conservative wing of the Soviet leadership, the KGB, and the army aimed at halting the USSR's disintegration and holding the republics by force. The State Committee for the State of Emergency declared: "to introduce a state of emergency in particular localities of the USSR for a term of 6 months from 4 a.m. Moscow time on August 19, 1991… to form the State Committee for the State of Emergency in the USSR"[1]. The putsch's failure opened the way to independence: the Act of Declaration was adopted "proceeding from the mortal danger that had loomed over Ukraine in connection with the coup d'état in the USSR on August 19, 1991"[2].

|---|
| **[Staging a Coup (T0020)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/328):** An armed seizure of power: the GKChP statement of 18 August 1991 announced the transfer of the USSR president's powers: "In connection with the impossibility, for reasons of health, of Mikhail Sergeevich Gorbachev performing the duties of President of the USSR and the transfer… of the powers of the President of the USSR to Vice-President Gennady Ivanovich Yanayev… to form the State Committee for the State of Emergency in the USSR"[1]. Gas supplies were cut off at the height of winter: "at 10.00am Moscow time on January 1, 2006, Gazprom cut off gas supplies to Ukraine"[1], and three years later "Russian exports to Ukraine were cut off on 1 January. # Campaign: Diplomatic Attack Against NATO Enlargement (2008) (C0098)

Diplomatic blackmail by V. Putin around the NATO summit in Bucharest aimed at blocking the granting of a Membership Action Plan (MAP) to Ukraine. Two days after the summit, at a meeting with G. Bush in Sochi, the Russian leader denied Ukrainian statehood - Ukraine, in his words, "is not a nation built in a natural manner" but "an artificial country created back in Soviet times"[1] - and directly threatened its rupture: "the country could just split apart," adding that, relying on anti-NATO forces, "Russia would be creating problems there all the time"[1]. At the summit itself, as retold by Kommersant's source, Putin told Bush: "You understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state!" - in effect threatening "that Russia could begin the severance of Crimea and Eastern Ukraine"[2].

---

| Procedures Carried Out |

| **[Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back (T0039)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/344):** An attempt to strike a deal with the US leader over Kyiv's head in order to block Ukraine's Euro-Atlantic integration under the threat of its dismemberment: Ukraine's accession to NATO would create "a field of conflict for you and us, long-term confrontation," while Moscow, relying on anti-NATO forces, "would be working on stripping NATO of the possibility of enlarging. Russia would be creating problems there all the time"[1]. As retold by Kommersant's source from the summit itself: "You understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state! What is Ukraine? Part of its territory is Eastern Europe, and part - a considerable part - was gifted by us!" - with a transparent hint "that Russia could begin the severance of Crimea and Eastern Ukraine"[2]. |

In 1956, the Crimean peninsula was transferred to Ukraine"[1]. From this the thesis of its possible disintegration was derived: "the country could just split apart"[1]. |

# Campaign: Derailing the Association with the EU (2013–2014) (C0099)

Economic and political pressure by V. Putin on V. Yanukovych in the autumn of 2013 aimed at derailing the signing of the Association Agreement with the EU. The price was formalized publicly on December 17, 2013: "Ukraine will receive 15 billion dollars from Russia and gas at a reduced price" - the gas price was lowered "to 268.5 dollars per thousand cubic meters" instead of the previous 410, and the money came "from the Russian National Welfare Fund" in exchange for Ukrainian government securities[1]. The refusal to sign the agreement triggered the protests: "between 21 November 2013 and 22 February 2014 large-scale street protests took place, provoked by the decision of then-President Viktor Yanukovych not to sign the association agreement with the European Union," and their suppression ended in shootings - on the Maidan "between January and February 2014 more than 100 people were killed, including by snipers"[2].

Putin stressed: "We consider this a temporary solution, bearing in mind that long-term, long-lasting agreements must and will be reached"[1]. |

# Campaign: Beginning of the Russo-Ukrainian War: Armed Invasion and Occupation of Crimea (2014) (C0100)

A covert military invasion and the occupation of Crimea, the beginning of Russia's armed aggression against Ukraine: the seizure of administrative buildings by troops without insignia, the installation of a controlled prime minister, and a sham referendum that the UN General Assembly declared void: "the referendum held in the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol on 16 March 2014, having no validity, cannot form the basis for any alteration of the status"[1]. The legal formalization of the seizure was completed in Moscow by the law of March 21, 2014[2].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (6)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The use of regular troops without insignia to establish control over the peninsula. A year later V. Putin admitted it on his call-in show of 17 April 2014: "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood. They acted very correctly, but… decisively and professionally"[3]. Ukrainian garrisons on the peninsula were blockaded and disarmed, as Putin himself admitted: "and the way the Ukrainian units were disarmed - all of this was done so swiftly that it seemed it had been prepared for an incredibly long time"[3]. |
| **[Disinformation (T0137)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/409):** The official denial of Russian troops' participation during the operation – and Putin's later admission (call-in show, 17 April 2014) that the denial was a lie: "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood"[3]. In the same broadcast an interlocutor congratulated him on having "honestly said that the 'little green men' are our peaceful military"[3]. |
| **[Puppet Government (T0037)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/342):** The installation of a controlled administration under military cover: the decisions of the Crimean parliament were taken in conditions where "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood"[3]. The UN General Assembly declared the ensuing referendum void and confirmed that it "was not authorized by Ukraine"[1]. OHCHR recorded the "election" scene itself: overnight into 27 February "armed groups without insignia took over the buildings of the local government and parliament," and "on 27 February, members of the Parliament of Crimea, in the presence of gunmen, dismissed the local Government and elected Sergey Aksenov as the Head of Crimea"[4]. |
| **[Sham Expression of Popular Will (T0109)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** The manufacturing of an appearance of mass pro-Russian mobilization on the peninsula: behind the "self-defense forces," in whose name the operation was conducted, stood Russian troops, as Putin admitted on 17 April 2014: "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood"[3]. Rally and "volunteer" crowds supplied the picture of a popular impulse whose legal significance the UN rejected[1]. |
| **[Sham Expression of Popular Will (T0109)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** The sham referendum of March 16, 2014 under military occupation: the UN General Assembly noted that it "was not authorized by Ukraine" and determined that it, "having no validity, cannot form the basis for any alteration of the status of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea or of the city of Sevastopol"[1]. |
| **[Annexation of Territories (T0017)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/325):** The legal formalization of the territory's severance: the treaty on "accession" was signed on March 18, 2014, and the law ratifying it was "Adopted by the State Duma on March 20, 2014, approved by the Federation Council on March 21, 2014"[2]. |

</details>

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Continuation of the Russo-Ukrainian War: Armed Aggression in the Donbas (2014–2015) (C0101)

The expansion of Russian aggression through the seizure of administrative buildings in eastern Ukraine by armed detachments: "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices in towns and villages of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions"[1]. The commander of the detachment that crossed the border, I. Girkin ("Strelkov"), later admitted his own role: "It was I, after all, who pulled the trigger of the war. Had our detachment not crossed the border, it would all have ended as in Kharkiv, as in Odesa"[2]. The campaign was accompanied by terror against the local population, the downing of flight MH17, and massive disinformation[3]. In the summer of 2014, the Russian Federation brought in regular troops, which led to the battles near Ilovaisk and Debaltseve. The UN monitoring mission recorded bussed-in crowds from the outset: "people were brought in buses and paid to take part in protests and conduct them according to specific scenarios, including causing violent incidents," while "some protesters allegedly come from the Russian Federation"[4].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (13)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Proxy War (T0018)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/326):** The seizure of Sloviansk by an armed group that had crossed the border, and the formation of the separatist "DNR"/"LNR": the detachment's commander openly admitted that "in practice it was our detachment that set in motion the flywheel of the war that is still going on," and that "it was I, after all, who pulled the trigger of the war"[2]. In parallel, "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices"[1]. The "republic's" leadership was from the outset dispatched from Moscow: "Alexander Boroday - the first prime minister of the DNR, who in 2014 handed over his powers to Alexander Zakharchenko," a Muscovite raised "in an intelligentsia Moscow family"[5]. |
| **[Disinformation (T0137)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/409):** A massive campaign of fabricating fakes to dehumanize Ukrainians: on state television it was claimed that "Ukrainian armed forces herded city residents to the central square and publicly executed a small boy and his mother," yet "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim," and the residents of Sloviansk who were interviewed did not confirm the story[6]. The same method produced the fabricated "death of a 10-year-old girl" in the Petrovskyi district of Donetsk (March 2015): BBC correspondents on the ground established that no such girl had ever existed[7]. In parallel ran an operation to conceal responsibility for the destruction of flight MH17: the Russian Ministry of Defense "made a series of self-contradictory claims blaming Ukraine, rather than Russia or Russian-led separatists, for the Boeing 777's shoot down," while a deputy defense minister publicly repeated "a fabricated claim that originated on Twitter of how a Spanish air traffic controller named Carlos saw two Ukrainian fighter jets near MH17"[3]. |
| **[Cyber Operations (T0136)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/408):** The use of a hacker group linked to the security services to compromise Ukrainian artillerymen's software: "the filename 'Попр-Д30.apk' was linked to a legitimate application which was initially developed domestically within Ukraine by an officer of the 55th Artillery Brigade named Yaroslav Sherstuk," and "in-depth reverse engineering revealed the APK contained an Android variant of X-Agent" - an implant whose exclusive operator is FANCY BEAR[8]. The same toolkit was used in cyberattacks on the Ukrainian power grid in the winters of 2015 and 2016[9][10]. |
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The overt crossing of the state border by regular Russian troops in the summer and autumn of 2014 to save the separatists from defeat: the "DNR" commander admitted that the decisive role was played by Russian servicemen who came "on leave" - "it was mostly 'vacationers' who advanced on Mariupol. When they left, both the front line and the opportunities became precarious"[2]. The offensive resulted in heavy losses for the Ukrainian army near Ilovaisk and Debaltseve. The presence of regular troops continued into 2015: the GRU men captured near Shchastia were "soldiers of the 3rd Separate Guards Special Purpose Brigade of the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, who arrived on the territory of Ukraine on March 26 and were quartered in Luhansk"[11]. |
| **[Abduction of People (T0053)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/354):** Mass unlawful detentions and abductions of civilians in the occupied territories: "armed groups continued to commit abductions, to subject people to physical and psychological torture and ill-treatment," and "people were abducted for ransom, for forced labor, and for exchange for fighters captured by the Ukrainian authorities"[1]. |
| **[Torture and Abuse (T0110)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/370):** The systematic use of torture and physical violence against civilians for a pro-Ukrainian stance: the UN recorded that "armed groups continued to commit abductions, to subject people to physical and psychological torture and ill-treatment, and to commit other grave human rights violations"[1]. Abducted Automaidan activists were held in a basement where they were "allegedly beaten several times, with their hands bound," and their hair was cut off in reprisal[12]. |
| **[Neutralization of the Opposition (T0021)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/329):** The physical elimination of legitimate representatives of local government who resisted the occupation: "the mutilated body of Volodomyr Rybak, a member of the 'Batkivshchyna' party and deputy of the Municipal Council of Horlivka (Donetsk region), was found near the village of Raihorodok," and "Rybak was abducted on April 17 by pro-Russians, following a pro-Ukrainian gathering in Horlivka. He was then tortured and murdered"[12]. |
| **[Terror (T0022)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/330):** Engagement in combat operations of Russian neo-Nazi groups (such as the "Rusich" sabotage and reconnaissance group under the command of A. Milchakov), whose ringleaders openly called for unmotivated sadistic violence against civilians ("Slaughter the homeless, the puppies, and the children!")[13]. |
| **[Deprivation of Electricity and Heating (T0124)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/396):** Targeted cyberattacks by Russian security services on distribution substations of the Ukrainian power grid in the winters of 2015 and 2016, aimed at causing mass power outages for the civilian population[9][10]. |
| **[Staging a Coup (T0020)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/328):** An attempted armed seizure of power in the spring of 2014 by storming regional administrations: the UN recorded that already "in mid-April 2014" "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices in towns and villages of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions," and "in order to retain control of the seized areas these groups erected barricades and checkpoints"[1]. In Kharkiv the coup was quickly suppressed. |
| **[Sponsoring Domestic Radical Groups (T0014)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/323):** The instigation of armed clashes in Odesa on May 2, 2014: the UN records the violence committed "in Odesa on 2 May 2014 during clashes between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died, mostly supporters of the country's federalization," and notes that "no one has yet been held to account"[1]. The culmination was the fire in the Trade Union Building where activists had taken refuge: the UN monitoring mission listed among the key uninvestigated questions "what caused the fire in the Trade Union building" and "who are the perpetrators of the killings"[14]. |
| **[Proxy War (T0018)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/326):** The use of armed formations to seize Mariupol in the spring and summer of 2014: as the "DNR" commander admitted, "it was mostly 'vacationers' who advanced on Mariupol" - that is, Russian servicemen - and after their departure "both the front line and the opportunities became precarious"[2]. The attempt to establish control over the city failed - on June 13 it was retaken by Ukrainian forces. |
| **[Aggressor Claiming Victim Status (T0005)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/315):** The exploitation of the Odesa tragedy to build a state propaganda myth and invert the roles: the actual picture, per the UN, is clashes "between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died," while the investigation remains incomplete and "no one has yet been held to account"[1]. The tragedy was used as moral justification for further aggression - by the same device as the "crucified boy" fake, for which "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim"[6]. |

</details>

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Ideological Preparation for the Full-Scale Invasion (2020–2021) (C0102)

A period of intensive ideological conditioning of Russian society and the political elite to justify the complete destruction of Ukrainian statehood. The head of the Russian state published a programmatic article declaring that "Russians and Ukrainians are one people, a single whole," and wrote of the Bolsheviks that "the Bolsheviks' actions in severing from Russia its historical territories are not considered a criminal act"[1]. Deputy Security Council chairman D. Medvedev (Kommersant, 11 October 2021) declared negotiations with Kyiv pointless: "it is pointless for us to deal with vassals. One must do business with the suzerain"[2]. In parallel came the indoctrination of the army and military blackmail through the massing of troops near the borders under the guise of exercises[3].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (4)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Rewriting of History (T0004)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/314):** The publication of the manifesto "On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians" (July 2021), constructing a pseudo-historical myth: "Russians and Ukrainians are one people, a single whole," while modern borders are declared the result of the fact that "the Bolsheviks' actions in severing from Russia its historical territories are not considered a criminal act"[1]. The same article describes how Lenin personally "persuaded" the leaders of the Donetsk-Kryvyi Rih republic "to act within Soviet Ukraine," and how the Central Committee resolved "to create at the congress 'one government for all of Ukraine'"[1]. On the eve of the invasion the thesis was taken to its limit: in his address of February 21, 2022 Putin declared that "modern Ukraine was entirely and wholly created by Russia, or, to be more precise, by Bolshevik, communist Russia," and called the country "Ukraine named after Vladimir Ilyich Lenin" - "He is its author and architect"[4]. |
| **[Deprivation of Agency (T0008)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/318):** The official denial of the Ukrainian nation's right to independent statehood: the article by the head of the Russian state declares outright that "Ukraine's genuine sovereignty is possible precisely in partnership with Russia," while "the wall that has arisen in recent years between Russia and Ukraine" is declared a split of "between parts of what is essentially one historical and spiritual space"[1]. |
| **[Dehumanization (T0006)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/316):** An article by D. Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, in Kommersant (11 October 2021) marginalizing the Ukrainian leadership: "it is pointless for us to deal with vassals. One must do business with the suzerain"; "at the head of Ukraine stand weak people who strive only to line their own pockets," and negotiations with them are "absolutely pointless"[2]. In the same text the Ukrainian president was likened to a hypothetical Jew serving in the SS[2]. |
| **[Cultivation of a Logic of Superiority (T0003)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/313):** Total indoctrination of Russian society with the ideas of the philosopher I. Ilyin (so-called "white fascism") and the transformation of the "Russian World" concept into a state ideology (rashism) that justifies the metropole's cultural superiority and existential right to violence against its neighbors[3]. |

</details>

posts.markdown:
# Campaign: Full-Scale Invasion (from February 24, 2022) (C0103)

Open aggression and a large-scale military invasion of the territory of Ukraine by the Russian Federation from several directions: "On the same day, Russian troops crossed various border points into Ukraine, including through Belarus, and launched attacks by land, air and sea"[1]. The goal of the campaign is the complete destruction of Ukrainian statehood and the erasure of Ukrainian identity. The UN commission established that the violations "amount to war crimes and include wilful killings, attacks on civilians, unlawful confinement, torture, rape and the forced transfer and deportation of children," and that strikes were carried out "with an apparent disregard for civilian harm and suffering"[1]. The campaign is accompanied by the destruction of entire cities (urbicide), ecocide, and a systematic policy of assimilation in the occupied territories[2]. The OSCE mission found "clear patterns of IHL violations by the Russian forces in their conduct of hostilities": had they respected "their IHL obligations in terms of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack," civilian casualties would have been far lower[3].

…

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (17)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Military Intervention (T0019)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/327):** The invasion by the regular Russian army and massive missile and air strikes on Ukrainian cities: "On 24 February 2022, the President of the Russian Federation, Vladimir Putin, announced his decision to conduct a 'special military operation' in Ukraine to seek its 'demilitarization and denazification'. On the same day, Russian troops crossed various border points into Ukraine, including through Belarus, and launched attacks by land, air and sea"[1]. The UN Commission investigated the events of February-March 2022 in Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kharkiv and Sumy Provinces[1]. |
| **[Mass Killings of Civilians (T0104)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/365):** The deliberate killing of civilians in occupied territories: the UN commission established "a widespread pattern of summary executions in areas that the armed forces of the Russian Federation controlled in 17 localities of Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Kyiv and Sumy Provinces, with the highest number in Kyiv Province, including in the city of Bucha," confirming "the execution of 65 men, 2 women and a 14-year-old boy"; "in more than half of the executions investigated, witnesses had last seen the victims in the custody of the armed forces of the Russian Federation"[1]. |
| **[Total Destruction of Infrastructure (T0105)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/366):** The practice of "urbicide" - the deliberate erasure of entire Ukrainian cities (for example, Mariupol), the destruction of infrastructure, and the entombment of the dead in the foundations of ruins[2]. The blowing up of the Kakhovka dam on 6 June 2023: "the breach of the dam at the Kakhovska Hydroelectric Power Plant in June 2023 resulted in massive flooding downstream, triggering an environmental disaster that has already had catastrophic effects on communities across the region," while "the flooding killed 34 civilians (32 in Kherson region and 2 in Mykolaiv region)" on Ukrainian-controlled territory alone[17]. The scale of the disaster on the very first day: "about 16 thousand people on the right bank of Kherson region are in the critical zone," with 80 settlements under threat of flooding[18]. |
| **[Extermination on a Territorial Basis (T0118)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/391):** Deliberate mass killings of people without regard to their ethnic origin, solely on the basis of their Ukrainian citizenship and affiliation with the Ukrainian state[2]. |
| **[Disinformation (T0137)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/409):** Total information control and a ban on calling the invasion a war - officially it was declared a "special military operation" whose stated aims were "demilitarization and denazification"[1]. The informational cover for energy terror rested on the "response" narrative: "There is a lot of noise now about our strikes on the energy infrastructure of the neighboring country. Yes, we are doing this. But who started it?"[12]. |
| **[Nuclear Blackmail (T0138)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/410):** Nuclear blackmail and the armed seizure of nuclear facilities: the IAEA recorded that "a large number of Russian tanks and infantry 'broke through the block-post' to the town of Enerhodar, a few kilometres from the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant," while the Ukrainian regulator reported that "Russian infantry troops were moving directly towards the site of Ukraine's largest nuclear power plant," calling the situation "critical"[19]. International bodies also voiced concern about "the unacceptable nuclear rhetoric used by Russian officials"[1]. Already on February 24 the Chornobyl NPP was seized as well: Ukraine informed the IAEA that "Russian forces had taken control of the facilities of the State Specialized Enterprise Chornobyl NPP" within the Exclusion Zone[20]. |
| **[Deprivation of Electricity and Heating (T0124)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/396):** Систематические кибератаки на энергетические компании и муниципальные теплоснабжающие предприятия в условиях полномасштабной войны для прекращения подачи электроэнергии и тепла украинским гражданским потребителям[21][22]. |
| **[Cyber Operations (T0136)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/408):** Масштабные операции спецслужб РФ по кибершпионажу, перехвату данных (в том числе через взлом публичных сетей Wi-Fi) и скрытому развертыванию деструктивного ПО против украинских организаций и граждан[23][24]. |

Research by the Yale lab documents that "Russia's federal government is operating a large scale, systematic network of camps and other facilities that has held at least 6,000 children from Ukraine within Russia-occupied Crimea and mainland Russia during the past year"[25]. |
| **[Filtration Camp System (T0023)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/331):** The creation of a network of filtration camps in the occupied territories: "'filtration' is defined within the context of this report as the multi-step system Russia and its proxies have deployed in territory they currently occupy within Ukraine to register, interrogate, and, in some cases, indefinitely detain people residing there at the time Russia and its aligned forces took that locale under its control," and "there is evidence the system was created weeks before the invasion began and likely grew following Russia's capture of Mariupol in April 2022"[26]. |
| **[Erasure and Renaming of Place Names (T0043)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/347):** Deliberate restoration of old Soviet or imperial names to captured cities and streets (in particular, the renaming of Bakhmut to Artemovsk) in order to erase Ukrainian national memory and visually integrate them into the space of the Russian Federation. |
| **[Forced Passportization (T0035)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/340):** Coercing residents of the occupied territories into taking Russian passports: "the policy of mass conferral of Russian citizenship to residents of occupied areas of Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions exacerbated the coercive environment there," and "those who refused Russian passports were denied access to public services, notably social security, healthcare, and education, and risked unemployment" and "faced a heightened risk of arbitrary detention when crossing checkpoints"[17]. |
| **[Sham Expression of Popular Will (T0109)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/369):** The staging of sham "referendums" in the occupied territories in the autumn of 2022: the UN General Assembly noted that "the illegal so-called referendums were organized from 23 to 27 September 2022 in these regions as attempts to modify the internationally recognized borders of Ukraine," and determined that they "have no validity under international law and do not form the basis for any alteration of the status of these regions of Ukraine"[5]. |
| **[Migratory Replacement (T0117.001)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/389):** Artificial alteration of the demographic composition of the population in the occupied territories (for example, in destroyed Mariupol) by incentivizing the relocation of citizens of the Russian Federation and their mass purchase of housing, against the backdrop of squeezing out the indigenous residents. |
| **[Expropriation of Resources (T0052)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/353):** The large-scale plunder of the economic resources of the occupied territories: "from 2022 to 2025, almost 15 million tonnes of Ukrainian grain, valued at 6.8 billion US dollars, were illegally removed from the temporarily occupied districts of Ukraine"[27]. Strikes on port infrastructure were accompanied by "the destruction of grain and other products destined for export"[17]. The plunder extended to industry: "the owners of the stolen metal - the Azovstal, MMKI and Zaporizhstal plants - have already filed a series of criminal complaints"[28]. |
| **[Theft of Cultural Property (T0112)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/372):** The systematic plunder of historical and cultural heritage and the mass removal of museum collections: according to Ukraine's minister of culture, "one million seven hundred thousand items of our cultural heritage were stolen from the occupied territories – including archaeological artifacts and museum collections. The Russian Federation has unlawfully appropriated them, in clear violation of all norms of international law"[29]. The Council of Europe characterizes these attacks on cultural heritage as having a "genocidal dimension"[29]. |
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** From April 2022 the Russian occupation administrations marked the seized territories with imperial signs - in stone and on paper. In Kherson oblast more than 110 Lenin monuments had been dismantled before the invasion, with practically none left; after the occupation the invaders erected ten new ones: the first in Henichesk in April 2022 - the first Lenin monument on Ukrainian territory since 2014 - and at the end of that same month a monument was returned to its pedestal by the city council in Nova Kakhovka[30]. In Mariupol on 5 May 2022 a monument to a woman with a red flag was unveiled, and the ceremony was published in his Telegram channel by Andrei Turchak, secretary of the general council of "United Russia"; the Square of the Warrior-Liberators, named in honor of those who freed the city from the Nazis, was given back its Soviet name of "Lenin Komsomol Square" by the occupiers[31]. In parallel the occupation administration papered the territory with banners: in Kherson and Nova Kakhovka hung Russian-language billboards reading "Russia is here forever!," "Kherson - forever with Russia," "Kherson is a Russian city," and for them they bought, for twenty cents on a stock-photo site, a picture by the Ukrainian photographer Anna Pasichnyk - her son Yaroslav with a friend in vyshyvankas in a rapeseed field near Kyiv - painting a Russian flag in behind the children's backs[32]. In Balakliia in Kharkiv oblast the occupiers pasted over a city banner: first they hung "Ukraine and Russia are 'one'" on top of it, then a poster with a tricolor reading "We are one people with Russia!". On 10 September 2022 Ukrainian soldiers tore the tricolor down - and beneath it emerged the lines of Shevchenko that had stood there through the entire occupation: "Fight - and you shall prevail! God is helping you! Truth is with you, glory is with you, and holy freedom!"[33]. The signs held only until de-occupation: on 11 November 2022, a "Russia is here forever" poster in liberated Bilozerka in the Kherson region was torn down by local residents - the video was published by the Telegram channel "Nikolaevsky Vanek"[34]. |

</details>

posts.title: The "Historical Path" (1909–1911)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The "Historical Path" (1909–1911) (C0109)

The Kyiv section of the Imperial Russian Military-Historical Society was filling central Kyiv with monuments to "figures of Russian history" and pushed the Shevchenko monument, which the city had already decided to erect, off its allotted site. The queue of eight imperial monuments - from princess Olha to Nestor the chronicler - was submitted in a memorandum of 7 April 1910 by colonel Steletsky, the section's secretary[1]. The "historical path" program grew out of a letter from Zilov, the trustee of the educational district, to governor-general Trepov: Shevchenko should not be placed opposite a "Russian governmental institution," and "it would be necessary to erect a monument to one of the figures of Russian history"[1]. The only monument of the queue actually erected was princess Olha (4 September 1911) - on the site the city had allotted in 1909 for the Shevchenko monument and which the duma gave to the society in 1911, overturning its own decision[1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (1)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** In 1911 the Russian Empire erected a monument to princess Olha in Kyiv - on a site the city had allotted two years earlier for a monument to Shevchenko. In May 1909, the Kyiv city duma allotted the square on Mykhailivska Square for a monument to Taras Shevchenko[1]. Zilov, the trustee of the Kyiv educational district, wrote confidentially to governor-general Trepov that Shevchenko should not be placed opposite a "Russian governmental institution" and that "it would be necessary to erect a monument to one of the figures of Russian history"[1]. Out of this letter grew the program of the "historical path": on 7 April 1910, colonel Steletsky, secretary of the Kyiv section of the Imperial Russian Military-Historical Society, submitted a memorandum with a queue of eight monuments - princess Olha, Oleh, Yaroslav, Volodymyr, Volodymyr Monomakh, Sviatoslav, "prehistoric Kyiv" and Nestor the chronicler[1]. On 15 March 1911, the duma, with 68 of 72 councilors present, gave the society the site between St. Sophia Cathedral and St. Michael's Monastery - 46 votes against 22 - and at the same session overturned its own decision of 1909, moving the site of the future Shevchenko monument to the Karavaivska intersection: 41 against 24[1]. At first the duma rejected the concrete design as insufficiently "artistically monumental," and a month later permitted only a temporary model to be put up[1] - that is, they agreed to place a makeshift on the seized site, so long as it was occupied. The monument was unveiled on 4 September 1911: princess Olha in the center, to the left the apostle Andrew pointing at the Kyiv hills, to the right the seated Cyril and Methodius[2][3]. The model was sculpted by Ivan Kavaleridze and Petro Snitkin, the architect was Valerian Rykov, and the project was led by the sculptor Fedir Balavensky[4]; the historian Ihor Hyrych notes the paradox - the author of the imperial monument turned out to be "one of the 'Ukrainomaniacs' - a future outstanding sculptor and film director, and then a beginning artist, Ivan Kavaleridze"[5]. Cast on the pedestal was: "A Gift of the Sovereign Emperor to the City of Kyiv. In the Year of Our Lord 1911" - the tsar's cabinet did indeed give ten thousand rubles for the monument, and the Kyiv merchant Mohylevsky contributed another thousand[2][1]. Below, on the pedestal of the princess herself, stood: "She was the first from Rus to enter the Kingdom of Heaven; her the sons of Rus praise as their initiator"[2] - the baptism of Rus was being written into the imperial genealogy right on the stone. In 1919 the statue was thrown off its pedestal and buried, split in two, beneath the monument itself; in March 1923 the remaining figures were removed, and in March 1926 the communal department of Kyiv ordered the concrete cleared away for good[2][1]. In 1996 the statue was dug out from under the flowerbed and the monument was recreated from the old sketches, this time in marble[4]. |

</details>

posts.title: The Alexander II Monument in Kyiv (1911)
posts.markdown:
# Campaign: The Alexander II Monument in Kyiv (1911) (C0110)

In 1911 the Russian Empire erected in central Kyiv the largest monument to Alexander II in the entire empire. The gratitude on the pedestal was voiced not by Ukraine and not by Kyiv but by the "Southwestern Krai" - the empire's official name for the Ukrainian lands west of the Dnipro[1][2]. The monument was unveiled on 30 August 1911 on Tsarskaya Square; the money was raised by an all-Russian subscription, 200 thousand rubles; the central pedestal bore the coat of arms of the empire, the double-headed eagle, and the inscription "To the Tsar-Liberator, the grateful Southwestern Krai. The year 1911"[3][1].

---

<details><summary>**Procedures Carried Out (1)**</summary>

| Procedures Carried Out |
|---|
| **[Territorial Marking with Imperial Symbols (T0158)](https://t.me/decolonialist_en/602):** The Russian Empire erected in Kyiv the largest monument to Alexander II in the entire empire. The gratitude on the pedestal was voiced not by Ukraine and not by Kyiv but by the "Southwestern Krai" - the empire's official name for the Ukrainian lands west of the Dnipro[2]. The monument, by the Italian sculptor Ximenes, was unveiled on 30 August 1911 on Tsarskaya Square, between the entrance to the Merchants' Garden and the building of the Merchants' Assembly; the unveiling was timed to the fiftieth anniversary of the abolition of serfdom and held in the presence of emperor Nicholas II, the Bulgarian tsar Ferdinand and prime minister Stolypin, who two days later, on the evening of 1 September, was mortally wounded in the Kyiv theater[3]. The money for the monument was raised by an all-Russian subscription, 200 thousand rubles[1]. The central pedestal bore the coat of arms of the empire, the double-headed eagle, and the inscription "To the Tsar-Liberator, the grateful Southwestern Krai. The year 1911"; on the lower pedestal was a bas-relief of peasants giving thanks for the abolition of serfdom[1]. The krai comprised the Kyiv, Volyn and Podillia governorates[2], which after the suppression of the Polish uprising of 1830-1831 were merged into the Kyiv governorate-general (1832-1914), whose task, according to the Encyclopedia of the History of Ukraine, "consisted in the liquidation of the political, socio-ethnic and cultural distinctions of the krai and the intensification of the russification of its elite - the szlachta"[4]. The monument joined a row: the Kyiv Nicholas I (1896), Alexander III (1909), Alexander II (1911), Stolypin (1912) - the historian Ihor Hyrych calls this the pre-revolutionary monument boom and adds that the erection of the monument to princess Olha and the planned subsequent monuments were handled by the Kyiv section of the Imperial Russian Military-Historical Society, nine-tenths of which consisted of officers of the Kyiv military district, and its secretary, colonel Steletsky, in a memorandum to the governor-general of 7 April 1910, laid out the queue of future sculptures - from Olha and Oleh to Nestor the chronicler[5]. Hyrych sums up the outcome of those same years thus: in that time the Ukrainians put forward one monument, to Shevchenko, and were not allowed to erect it, while their opponents managed to put up "at least half a dozen monuments asserting Russianness and negating the Ukrainian national idea"[5]. |

</details>
